# Command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/reference-docs.sh from the code. Do not edit by hand: change the code and run scripts/reference-docs.sh (the pre-commit hook fails when this file is stale). -->

Every action in Regista is a command: the app's buttons and menus, `regista-engine exec` and Claude through MCP run the same ones. This page lists the 159 commands of the registry the MCP server describes its tools from.

- **MCP tool**: the tool name Claude sees (the id with `_` for `.`). Commands marked human-only are not MCP tools: the MCP server does not list them and refuses them; the person at the Mac runs them in the app (or with `regista-engine exec`).
- **Takes `project`**: every command but `project.new`, `project.open` and `project.list` also accepts `project`, a tab id from `project.list` ("tab-2") or a `.regista` path; without it the command acts on the tab the user sees.
- **Undo**: whether `history.undo` can take the command back. A command that fails changes nothing.
- **Times** are seconds on the timeline and snap to the frame grid. **Default** is what the parameter's description says.
- **Title** is the command's name in the app's English interface (activity log, history, status bar).

## adjust

### `adjust.set`

**Adjust the colour** · MCP tool: `adjust_set` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Photos-style adjustments on clips or — with no clip — the whole picture: exposure, brilliance, highlights, shadows, contrast, saturation, warmth, tint (each −1…1, 0 = untouched), sharpness and vignette (0…1). Only the values passed change; reset: true clears them first. keyframes animate any of them (or the look intensity, "amount") over timeline time: {"exposure": [{time, value, easing}]}. Returns the grade.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | no | the whole picture | Clip (default: the whole picture). |
| `clipIds` | array of string | no | – | Several clips. |
| `reset` | boolean | no | – | Set every adjustment back to 0 (and drop their keyframes) before applying the values passed. |
| `keyframes` | object | no | – | Per property: [{time (timeline s), value, easing}] — replaces that property's keyframes; [] removes them. |
| `exposure` | number | no | – | Esposizione: −1…1. |
| `brilliance` | number | no | – | Brillantezza: −1…1. |
| `highlights` | number | no | – | Luci: −1…1. |
| `shadows` | number | no | – | Ombre: −1…1. |
| `contrast` | number | no | – | Contrasto: −1…1. |
| `saturation` | number | no | – | Saturazione: −1…1. |
| `warmth` | number | no | – | Calore: −1…1. |
| `tint` | number | no | – | Tinta: −1…1. |
| `sharpness` | number | no | – | Nitidezza: 0…1. |
| `vignette` | number | no | – | Vignettatura: 0…1. |

Returns: the grade.

## audio

### `audio.addMusic`

**Add music** · MCP tool: `audio_addMusic` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Lay a music bed on its own track (Music, A2), levelled to a loudness (default −22 LUFS un-ducked), looped to the end if short, faded in/out, and ducked automatically under the voice: the speech regions of the voice track (its words) lower it by `duck` dB (default −12, so the music sits ~19 dB under a −15 LUFS voice while someone speaks) with smooth attack/release. House rule: no music unless asked (Instagram trending audio is added in the app); when used, keep it subtle. Returns the track, clips, gain and the expected level under speech.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Music file (wav/flac/mp3/m4a). |
| `start` | seconds | no | 0 | Timeline start (default 0). |
| `end` | seconds | no | the end of the timeline | Timeline end (default: the end of the timeline). |
| `sourceIn` | seconds | no | 0 | Start inside the music (default 0). |
| `level` | number | no | -22 | Loudness of the bed without ducking, LUFS (default -22). |
| `duck` | number | no | -12 | Gain under speech, dB (default -12; 0 = no ducking). |
| `attack` | number | no | 0.15 | Seconds to go down before a phrase (default 0.15). |
| `release` | number | no | 0.45 | Seconds to come back after it (default 0.45). |
| `mergeGap` | number | no | 0.7 | Pauses shorter than this stay ducked, seconds (default 0.7). |
| `voiceTrackId` | string | no | the voice track | Track that triggers the ducking (default: the voice track). |
| `fadeIn` | seconds | no | 0.5 | Fade-in seconds (default 0.5). |
| `fadeOut` | seconds | no | 1.5 | Fade-out seconds at the end (default 1.5). |
| `loop` | boolean | no | true | Repeat the music to fill the range (default true). |

Returns: the track, clips, gain and the expected level under speech.

### `audio.checkDucking`

**Check the music ducking** · MCP tool: `audio_checkDucking` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Measure the music under the voice: renders the voice and the music stems through the export mix (gains, fades, ducking envelope) and compares their loudness while someone speaks (inside the speech regions) and in the longer pauses. Pass: music at least minUnder dB (default 15) under the voice during speech. Returns both levels and the difference.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the music track | Music track (default: the music track). |
| `minUnder` | number | no | 15 | Required dB under the voice during speech (default 15). |

Returns: both levels and the difference.

### `audio.clean`

**Clean the voice** · MCP tool: `audio_clean` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Make the voice broadcast-ready after edit.autoCut: DeepFilterNet denoise + voice chain (per-take level match, per-segment level match — a second voice off the microphone more than 6 dB under the speaker is raised toward it, at most 12 dB —, EQ, gate, compressor, one linear normalization to −15 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.5 dBTP). The cleaned file becomes a new asset and replaces the source on the track's clips with the same ranges, so sync is unchanged. Re-run after a new edit.autoCut; restore: true puts the original sound back. Returns the loudness, the A/V lag and the commands it ran.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the first audio track | Audio track to clean (default: the first audio track). |
| `attenuation` | number | no | 18 | DeepFilterNet attenuation limit, dB (default 18). |
| `target` | number | no | -15 | Integrated loudness target, LUFS (default -15). |
| `truePeak` | number | no | -1.5 | True-peak ceiling, dBTP (default -1.5). |
| `gate` | boolean | no | true | Gentle gate in the chain (default true). |
| `levelMatch` | number | no | 6 | Speech segments further than this from the main speaker are gained toward it, dB (default 6; 0 = off): a second voice off the microphone. |
| `levelMatchMax` | number | no | 12 | Largest level-match gain, dB (default 12). |
| `restore` | boolean | no | – | Put the original sound back on the track's clips (same ranges, edge fades kept): the cleaning switched off, one undo step. Needs no engine. |

Returns: the loudness, the A/V lag and the commands it ran.

### `audio.duck`

**Duck the music under the voice** · MCP tool: `audio_duck` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Change (or remove) the automatic ducking of an audio track: which track triggers it, depth, attack, release, merge gap. Returns the track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | yes | – | The track to duck (the music). |
| `voiceTrackId` | string | no | the current one, or the voice track | Trigger track (default: the current one, or the voice track). |
| `duck` | number | no | – | Gain under speech, dB (0 removes the ducking). |
| `attack` | number | no | – | Seconds. |
| `release` | number | no | – | Seconds. |
| `mergeGap` | number | no | – | Seconds. |

Returns: the track.

## brandkit

### `brandkit.apply`

**Apply the brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_apply` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Apply a brand kit to the project in one go: its title presets become available to title.add, colour/font roles (primary, ink, paper, accent, success, highlight; display, text, mono) resolve in title params, captions are recoloured (keyword box = the kit's highlight, its text = onHighlight; the caption style the user chose — preset, font, size — is kept), titles made from presets are rebuilt in the new kit, and logo overlays (logo.add) are swapped for the new kit's logo and placement. The project keeps its own copy of the kit, its font files and logos included (copied into the project's media folder): deleting or changing the kit later does not change the video. Missing font files fall back to system fonts (reported). Run it before adding titles, and again any time to switch kit. Returns what was restyled.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | no | – | Kit id (arkad, wesites, cafe-atelier, or a user kit). |
| `path` | string | no | – | A kit folder, kit.json or older kit JSON file instead. |
| `captions` | boolean | no | true | Restyle the caption tracks with the kit's caption style (default true). |

Returns: what was restyled.

### `brandkit.check`

**Check the brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_check` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Check the applied brand kit on the edit: fonts (each role resolved or its system fallback), captions (style keyword box colour = the kit's highlight, and the rendered keyword box pixels on the first keyword's frame), logo overlays inside their safe zone (Instagram limits, out of the caption band), and titles, cards and labels whose text, box or highlight colour is none of the kit's colours (each named with its clip and time). Optionally writes the checked frame. Returns pass and the details.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | – | Write the frame checked (the first keyword's) to this .png. |
| `tolerance` | number | no | 12 | Max RGB distance between rendered and expected keyword box colour (default 12). |

Returns: pass and the details.

### `brandkit.create`

**Create a brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_create` · undo: yes — history.undo puts the brand kit back · takes `project`

Create a brand kit for a client (e.g. a bakery, a studio): a copy of an existing kit (from) with a new id and name, or — without from — the default kit's colours, fonts and placement with no logo (a new brand never starts with another brand's logo), then the given colours, fonts, caption style, logo placement, title presets. Saved as a folder (kit.json + assets) in the user's brand kits. Add the logo with brandkit.setLogo and font files with brandkit.setFont. Returns the kit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | – | Display name ("Café Atelier"). |
| `id` | string | no | from the name | Kit id (lowercase, digits, -; default from the name). |
| `from` | string | no | – | Kit to copy whole, logos included. Without it, the new kit takes the arkad kit's colours, fonts and placement, with no logo. |
| `colors` | object | no | – | Colour roles to set {role: #RRGGBB} (null removes): primary, accent, ink, paper, surface, success, highlight (caption keyword box, highlighted words), onHighlight (text on it). |
| `fonts` | object | no | – | Font roles {display, text, textBold, mono: font name or file} (files: prefer brandkit.setFont, which copies them into the kit). |
| `captionStyle` | object | no | – | Caption style fields to override (captions.setStyle names; colours may be roles), null removes one. |
| `logoPlacement` | object | no | – | {corner: topLeft\|topRight\|topCenter\|bottomLeft\|bottomRight, width (px at 1080), margin, opacity, animation, variant}. |
| `titles` | object | no | – | Title presets to add or replace {name: title fields as in project.state}, null removes one. |
| `watermark` | boolean | no | – | brandkit.apply also lays the logo over the whole video. |
| `notes` | string | no | – | How the brand moves and what to avoid. |

Returns: the kit.

### `brandkit.delete`

**Delete a brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_delete` · undo: yes — history.undo puts the brand kit back · takes `project`

Delete a user brand kit folder (a built-in with the same id shows again). Built-ins cannot be deleted. Returns the id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | yes | – | Kit id. |

Returns: the id.

### `brandkit.export`

**Export a brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_export` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Export a brand kit as one .registakit file (a zip of kit.json + logos + fonts, self-contained) to send to a partner, who adds it with brandkit.import or the app's Importa button. Returns the file.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | yes | – | Kit id. |
| `path` | string | yes | – | Output file (.registakit added if missing) or folder. |

Returns: the file.

### `brandkit.import`

**Import a brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_import` · undo: yes — history.undo puts the brand kit back · takes `project`

Add a brand kit from a .registakit file (from brandkit.export), a kit folder or a kit JSON. A kit with the id of an existing user kit gets a new id unless replace is true; a kit with a built-in's id replaces the built-in. Returns the kit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | The .registakit file, kit folder or kit JSON. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | false | Replace a user kit with the same id (default false). |

Returns: the kit.

### `brandkit.list`

**List brand kits** · MCP tool: `brandkit_list` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

List the brand kits: built-in arkad, wesites, cafe-atelier, plus the user's kits (folders in ~/Library/Application Support/Regista/brandkits). Each: colours by role, fonts (resolved or system fallback), logos (variants, found or not), logo placement, caption colours, title presets, motion notes, and whether it is built in or a user kit. Returns the kits and the project's active kit.

No parameters.

Returns: the kits and the project's active kit.

### `brandkit.preview`

**Brand kit preview** · MCP tool: `brandkit_preview` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Render a 9:16 preview of a brand kit through the real compositor: a caption with its keyword box, a hook title in the kit's display font, the logo at its placement, over a frame of the open project (or a backdrop in the kit's colours). Does not change the project. Returns the PNG and the fonts used.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | no | the applied kit | Kit id (default: the applied kit). |
| `definition` | object | no | – | A whole kit as JSON (unsaved edits, absolute asset paths) instead of an id. |
| `path` | string | no | a temporary file | Output .png (default: a temporary file). |
| `width` | integer | no | 540 | Width in px (default 540; height 16:9 of it). |
| `time` | seconds | no | a third in | Project time for the backdrop frame (default: a third in). |
| `title` | string | no | the kit's name | Title text (default: the kit's name). |
| `backdrop` | boolean | no | true | Use a frame of the open project behind (default true). |

Returns: the PNG and the fonts used.

### `brandkit.setFont`

**Change the kit's font** · MCP tool: `brandkit_setFont` · undo: yes — history.undo puts the brand kit back · takes `project`

Import a font file (.ttf, .otf, .woff2) into a brand kit folder and assign it to a role: display (titles), text, textBold, mono (labels). A kit whose font file goes missing falls back to a system font. Returns the kit with its fonts resolved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | yes | – | Kit id. |
| `path` | string | yes | – | The font file. |
| `role` | string | yes | – | display, text, textBold or mono (or a new role). |

Returns: the kit with its fonts resolved.

### `brandkit.setLogo`

**Change the kit's logo** · MCP tool: `brandkit_setLogo` · undo: yes — history.undo puts the brand kit back · takes `project`

Give a brand kit its logo: an SVG (preferred: sharp at any size) or a PNG with transparency, copied into the kit folder as a variant — onDark (light-coloured logo for footage, the default), onLight (dark-coloured logo for pale backgrounds) or mark (symbol only). Returns the kit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | yes | – | Kit id. |
| `path` | string | yes | – | The .svg or .png file. |
| `variant` | one of `onDark`, `onLight`, `mark` | no | – | onDark (default), onLight or mark. |

Returns: the kit.

### `brandkit.update`

**Edit the brand kit** · MCP tool: `brandkit_update` · undo: yes — history.undo puts the brand kit back · takes `project`

Change a brand kit: name, colours by role (merged; null removes), fonts, caption style, logo placement (corner, width, margin, opacity, animation, variant), title presets, watermark, notes. Updating a built-in saves a user copy with the same id that replaces it. The project keeps its applied copy until brandkit.apply is run again. history.undo puts the kit back as it was. Returns the kit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kit` | string | yes | – | Kit id. |
| `name` | string | no | – | Display name. |
| `colors` | object | no | – | Colour roles to set {role: #RRGGBB} (null removes): primary, accent, ink, paper, surface, success, highlight (caption keyword box, highlighted words), onHighlight (text on it). |
| `fonts` | object | no | – | Font roles {display, text, textBold, mono: font name or file} (files: prefer brandkit.setFont, which copies them into the kit). |
| `captionStyle` | object | no | – | Caption style fields to override (captions.setStyle names; colours may be roles), null removes one. |
| `logoPlacement` | object | no | – | {corner: topLeft\|topRight\|topCenter\|bottomLeft\|bottomRight, width (px at 1080), margin, opacity, animation, variant}. |
| `titles` | object | no | – | Title presets to add or replace {name: title fields as in project.state}, null removes one. |
| `watermark` | boolean | no | – | brandkit.apply also lays the logo over the whole video. |
| `notes` | string | no | – | How the brand moves and what to avoid. |

Returns: the kit.

## callout

### `callout.add`

**Add a callout** · MCP tool: `callout_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Draw attention to something on screen with a hand-drawn callout that draws itself on: arrow (from → to), circle, underline, box (rounded rectangle) or highlight (translucent marker band). Coordinates are pixels of the project frame (1080×1920 for a reel, 1920×1080 for a screen recording). Colour defaults to the brand kit's accent. Fades out at the end. Taste: one callout at a time, on the thing the voice is talking about; tutorials: on clicks. Returns the clip and warnings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `arrow`, `circle`, `underline`, `box`, `highlight` | yes | – | Callout shape. |
| `start` | seconds | yes | – | Timeline start. |
| `duration` | seconds | no | 2 | Seconds on screen (default 2). Left out, the graphic ends with the main video at the latest: shortened, or started earlier to keep 1 s (the result's timing says so). |
| `end` | seconds | no | – | Timeline end instead of duration. |
| `rect` | array of number | no | – | [x, y, w, h] of the thing to mark, pixels of the project frame (circle, underline, box, highlight). |
| `from` | array of number | no | – | arrow: tail [x, y], pixels. |
| `to` | array of number | no | – | arrow: head [x, y], pixels. |
| `color` | string | no | the kit's accent, else #FFD43B | #RRGGBB or a brand colour role (default: the kit's accent, else #FFD43B). |
| `width` | number | no | 10 | Stroke width, px at 1080 wide (default 10; highlight ignores it). |
| `drawOn` | number | no | 0.45 | Seconds to draw it on (default 0.45; 0 = appears whole). |
| `trackId` | string | no | a free one | Overlay track (default: a free one). |

Returns: the clip and warnings.

## captions

### `captions.checkFaces`

**Check captions against the face** · MCP tool: `captions_checkFaces` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Verify that no caption covers a face: on every frame a chunk shows, each word drawn (ink box, at its band and shift) against the caption zone of every face on the picture (head + some neck; a child in the arms too), from the face track through the clip crops. Run it after captions.generate (and after any crop change). Fails on any overlap. Returns pass, frames and chunks checked, and each overlap (chunk, time, boxes).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one with captions | Caption track (default: the first one with captions). |

Returns: pass, frames and chunks checked, and each overlap (chunk, time, boxes).

### `captions.checkTiming`

**Check caption timing** · MCP tool: `captions_checkTiming` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Verify the captions in an exported mp4: for every word, the first frame where it is visibly there vs the frame of its timeline word start (pass = within ±1 frame), and whether every word box lies inside the caption band. Run it on the final export. Returns pass, errors per word and the band check.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Rendered video (export.render output, same preset). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one with captions | Caption track (default: the first one with captions). |
| `preset` | one of `9:16`, `4:5`, `1:1`, `16:9` | no | the project size | 9:16 (1080×1920), 4:5 (1080×1350, feed portrait), 1:1 (1080×1080) or 16:9 (1920×1080); another aspect than the project's reframes every clip by crop (default: the project size). |
| `window` | integer | no | 6 | Search ±frames around each expected reveal (default 6). |
| `tolerance` | integer | no | 1 | Frames of error still passing (default 1). |

Returns: pass, errors per word and the band check.

### `captions.clear`

**Remove captions from a stretch** · MCP tool: `captions_clear` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Take the captions off a stretch of time (the opening title, the closing logo): a chunk inside it goes, a chunk that crosses its start ends there, a chunk that crosses its end starts there with the words still being spoken. One undo step (captions.generate rebuilds them all). Returns the chunks removed and shortened.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | seconds | yes | – | Start of the stretch. |
| `to` | seconds | yes | – | End of the stretch. |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one with captions | Caption track (default: the first one with captions). |

Returns: the chunks removed and shortened.

### `captions.generate`

**Generate captions** · MCP tool: `captions_generate` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Add the burned-in captions: word-by-word chunks built from the transcript of the edited timeline, on a caption track (created if missing), in a style preset (talking-head-v1 = the approved look), with your keywords on a pink box (default: the script's keywords from script.prepare) and fixes for misheard words. Run it after the picture edit is final (re-run after any cut: captions go stale). Re-running keeps the track's keywords, fixes and style unless new ones are given. Returns chunk/word counts, how many keywords are shown and a preview of the first chunks.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one, created if missing | Caption track (default: the first one, created if missing). |
| `sourceTrackId` | string | no | the first video track with clips | Track whose words are captioned (default: the first video track with clips). |
| `keywords` | array of string | no | – | Keywords (display form, e.g. uppercase). |
| `keywordsPath` | string | no | – | keywords.json with {"keywords": [...], "fixes": {...}}. |
| `fixes` | object | no | – | Replacements of displayed words, {"AL": "ALL'IA", "IA": ""} (empty removes the word). |
| `style` | one of `talking-head-v1`, `elegant-serif`, `bold-keyword`, `ghost-karaoke` | no | talking-head-v1 | Style preset (default talking-head-v1; elegant-serif, bold-keyword, ghost-karaoke: effects.catalog category captions). |
| `avoidFaces` | boolean | no | true | Move chunks off every face of the picture (needs faces.track; default true): another band inside the Instagram safe zones, shifted aside, or split shorter. |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | – | Change nothing: return the chunks it would build and suggestedKeywords (the keywords it would use, then numbers, names and the longest word of each sentence, never stop words) for a person to accept or edit before generating. |

Returns: chunk/word counts, how many keywords are shown and a preview of the first chunks.

### `captions.get`

**Read the captions** · MCP tool: `captions_get` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Proof-read the captions: every chunk with its words, timeline times and keyword flags, the keywords, fixes and style, and whether they are stale (the timeline changed since captions.generate). Returns that list.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one with captions | Caption track (default: the first one with captions). |

Returns: that list.

### `captions.place`

**Move the captions** · MCP tool: `captions_place` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Move or resize the captions by hand, like text in an Instagram story: the whole track (default) or only some chunks (chunk index, chunks, the chunk showing at time, or every chunk starting in from…to). x is the line's left edge, centre or right edge (align), y the vertical centre of the line, in pixels of the frame (1080×1920) — or dx/dy to move from where it is now; scale resizes (1 = the style's size). A chunk's own placement wins over the track's; a chunk placed by hand stays there (automatic face avoidance leaves it alone; captions.checkFaces reports a face under it as a warning). reset goes back to automatic. Lines are kept inside the frame. Returns where each line now is and warnings for the Instagram zones.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one with captions | Caption track (default: the first one with captions). |
| `chunk` | integer | no | – | Only this chunk (index from captions.get). |
| `chunks` | array of integer | no | – | Only these chunks. |
| `time` | seconds | no | – | Only the chunk showing at this timeline time (seconds). |
| `from` | seconds | no | – | Only the chunks starting at or after this time (with to). |
| `to` | seconds | no | – | …and before this time. |
| `x` | number | no | – | Horizontal position: the line's left edge (align left), centre (center, default) or right edge (right). |
| `y` | number | no | – | Vertical centre of the line. |
| `dx` | number | no | – | Move right by this much from the current position (negative = left). |
| `dy` | number | no | – | Move down by this much (negative = up). |
| `units` | one of `px`, `fraction` | no | – | x/y/dx/dy in pixels of the project frame (px, default; 1080×1920 for a reel) or fractions of its width/height (fraction). |
| `scale` | number | no | – | Size factor, 0.3…4 (1 = the style's size). |
| `align` | one of `left`, `center`, `right` | no | – | What x refers to: left, center or right edge of the line. |
| `reset` | boolean | no | – | Back to automatic (the track: every chunk too). With other fields: start from automatic, then apply them. |

Returns: where each line now is and warnings for the Instagram zones.

### `captions.setKeywords`

**Change the keywords** · MCP tool: `captions_setKeywords` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Change which words get the keyword box (display form, uppercase as shown): replace the list, add or remove words, or load a keywords.json (keywords and fixes; new fixes rebuild the chunks). Returns the caption summary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `keywords` | array of string | no | – | Replace the keyword list. |

| `remove` | array of string | no | – | Remove keywords. |

### `captions.setStyle`

**Change the caption style** · MCP tool: `captions_setStyle` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Apply a caption style preset (talking-head-v1 = the approved WeSites look; elegant-serif = cream serif italic, one calm phrase at a time; bold-keyword = bold white sans on up to two lines, keyword in the brand accent; ghost-karaoke = whole phrase shown, upcoming words ghosted, lit word by word — effects.catalog category captions says when to use each) and/or override fields: font, fontSize, strokeWidth, colors, gap, bandY, bandHeight, maxWords, maxChars, hold, reveal (word|chunk), keywordMode (box|color), upcomingOpacity, shadowOpacity/shadowBlur/shadowY, maxLineWidth, lineSpacing, wordAlign (center|baseline); null clears an optional field. Chunking fields rebuild the chunks. Only change the approved style when asked. Returns the caption summary.

## clip

### `clip.follow`

**Follow the face** · MCP tool: `clip_follow` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Make an overlay (sticker, logo, image, title) follow a tracked point of the speaker: target face (its centre or just above the head; needs faces.track) or hand (the palm, index tip or wrist; needs hands.track over the clip's window). Writes dense transform keyframes (every 2 frames, smoothed), keeping the clip's own animation, so it stays an ordinary undoable edit. For an object held in the hand: hover lifts it above the palm with a gentle float, spin turns it in depth (rotationY, or flat with spinAxis z), halo adds a glowing ellipse under it, openOnly shows it only while the palm is open (fading in and out). Returns the keyframes written and how much of the window the target was visible.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | – | The follower (a placed overlay: sticker, logo, image, title). |
| `target` | one of `face`, `hand` | yes | – | What it follows. |
| `assetId` | string | no | the main video under the clip | Tracked video asset (default: the main video under the clip). |
| `point` | one of `center`, `top`, `palm`, `index`, `wrist` | no | – | face: center (default) or top (above the head); hand: palm (default), index or wrist. |
| `hand` | one of `left`, `right`, `any` | no | any: the most open one | Which hand (default any: the most open one). |
| `openOnly` | boolean | no | true | hand: show only while the palm is open (default true). |
| `offset` | array of number | no | [0, 0] | [dx, dy] px at 1080×1920 from the point (default [0, 0]). |
| `hover` | number | no | 0 | Px above the point with a slow ±6 px float (default 0; 60–120 for an object over the palm). |
| `spin` | number | no | 0 = no spin | Seconds per turn (default 0 = no spin; 2.5 reads as a slow showcase turn). |
| `spinAxis` | one of `y`, `z` | no | – | y (default): turns in depth around its vertical axis, like a coin on a turntable; z: spins flat. |
| `halo` | boolean | no | false | Add a glowing ellipse under the object, following the point (default false). |
| `haloColor` | string | no | the kit's highlight, else #FFB066 | Halo colour (#RRGGBB or a brand role; default the kit's highlight, else #FFB066). |

Returns: the keyframes written and how much of the window the target was visible.

### `clip.keyframe`

**Clip animation** · MCP tool: `clip_keyframe` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Animate a clip's transform: apply an entrance/exit preset (pop, slideUp, slideDown, fade, kenBurns, none = remove) or set explicit keyframes with easing ({time (s from the clip start), scale, x, y, rotation, opacity, crop, easing: linear|easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|expoOut|backOut|hold|spring — the curve towards the next keyframe}). The clip's static transform is the resting state. Returns the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | no | – | Clip. |
| `clipIds` | array of string | no | – | Several clips. |
| `preset` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | – | Entrance and exit preset (or animIn/animOut separately). |
| `keyframes` | array of object | no | – | Explicit keyframes (replace existing ones). |
| `animIn` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | – | Entrance: pop (scale with overshoot), slideUp, slideDown, fade, kenBurns (slow push over the whole clip), none. |
| `animOut` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | same as animIn | Exit (default: same as animIn; kenBurns has none). |
| `inDuration` | number | no | 0.35 | Entrance seconds (default 0.35; fade 0.25). |
| `outDuration` | number | no | 0.25 | Exit seconds (default 0.25). |

Returns: the clip.

### `clip.place`

**Place the clip** · MCP tool: `clip_place` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Move, resize or rotate anything drawn on the frame by hand (what a drag on the preview does): a title, sticker, logo or overlay; the full-frame picture (a camera take, a full-frame insert: the first move turns "fills the frame" into a box exactly as large as the frame, then moves it; smaller than the frame, the background shows around it); a box of a recording layout (screen, camera bubble: a box placed by hand, until layout.apply is run again on it); a callout, progress bar, status row or level meters (their own rectangle moves and grows). x/y = where its centre goes, in pixels of the frame (1080×1920) — or dx/dy from where it is now — scale (titles, stickers, logos, overlays: 1 = native size; the others: 1 = the size it had before it was first moved by hand), rotation in degrees (not a callout). Its animation moves with it: entrance/exit, punch-ins and auto zoom (the crop is kept: the same part of the picture shows), follow. Kept inside the frame (a full-frame picture: its centre). reset puts it back exactly as it was before it was first moved. A motion template or a halo cannot be placed by hand. Returns its box and warnings (caption band, Instagram zones).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | – | The clip: a title, sticker, logo, overlay, full-frame picture, layout box, callout, progress bar, status row or meters (frame.elements lists them). |
| `x` | number | no | – | Horizontal centre. |
| `y` | number | no | – | Vertical centre. |
| `dx` | number | no | – | Move right by this much (negative = left). |
| `dy` | number | no | – | Move down by this much (negative = up). |
| `units` | one of `px`, `fraction` | no | – | x/y/dx/dy in pixels of the project frame (px, default; 1080×1920 for a reel) or fractions of its width/height (fraction). |
| `scale` | number | no | – | Size factor, 0.05…20 (titles, stickers, logos, overlays: 1 = native size; pictures, layout boxes, callouts: 1 = their size before the first move by hand). |
| `rotation` | number | no | – | Degrees clockwise (not callouts, progress bars, status rows or meters). |
| `reset` | boolean | no | – | Back to exactly how it was before it was first moved by hand. |

Returns: its box and warnings (caption band, Instagram zones).

### `clip.set`

**Edit the clip** · MCP tool: `clip_set` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Set clip properties on one clip, several, or every clip of a track (trackId): crop (source pixels [w, h, x, y], scaled to fill the frame), scale/x/y/rotation/opacity, keyframes (animated transform), grade (ffmpeg eq brightness/contrast/saturation; the house light grade is 0.02 / 1.06 / 1.08), audio edge fades and gain, picture fades (from / to black or transparent), a title's text, a motion template's fields and the amount of an applied effect. Unset properties are kept. Returns the changed clips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | no | – | One clip. |
| `clipIds` | array of string | no | – | Several clips. |
| `trackId` | string | no | – | Every clip of this track. |
| `crop` | array of number | no | – | Crop [w, h, x, y] in source display pixels (rotation applied, origin top-left). |
| `scale` | number | no | – | Extra zoom after filling the frame (1 = fill). |
| `x` | number | no | – | Horizontal offset of the centre, fraction of the output width. |
| `y` | number | no | – | Vertical offset of the centre, fraction of the output height (down is positive). |
| `rotation` | number | no | – | Degrees clockwise. |
| `opacity` | number | no | – | 0…1. |
| `anchorX` | number | no | 0.5 = centre | 2.5D: pivot of scale and rotations, fraction of the picture width (default 0.5 = centre; the picture does not move). |
| `anchorY` | number | no | – | 2.5D: pivot, fraction of the picture height (0 = top edge: a card hanging from its top). |
| `rotationX` | number | no | – | 2.5D: tilt in degrees around the horizontal axis (positive = the top goes away). |
| `rotationY` | number | no | – | 2.5D: turn in degrees around the vertical axis (positive = the right side goes away). |
| `perspective` | number | no | 2000 | 2.5D: camera distance, px at 1080 wide (default 2000; 800 = strong perspective). |
| `behindSwitches` | array of object | no | – | Switch the layer behind / in front of the person over time: [{time (s from the clip start), behind: true\|false}] (needs matte.track); [] removes them. |
| `keyframes` | array of object | no | – | Animated transform: [{time (s from clip start), crop?, scale?, x?, y?, rotation?, opacity?, anchorX?, anchorY?, rotationX?, rotationY?, perspective?, easing?}], each starting from the clip's transform; easing (linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut, expoOut, backOut, hold, spring) shapes the move to the next keyframe. Replaces existing keyframes (clip.keyframe has presets). |
| `clearKeyframes` | boolean | no | – | Remove the keyframes. |
| `brightness` | number | no | – | eq brightness −1…1 (0 = none). |
| `contrast` | number | no | – | eq contrast (1 = none). |
| `saturation` | number | no | – | eq saturation (1 = none). |
| `fadeIn` | seconds | no | – | Audio fade-in at the clip start, seconds (0 removes). |
| `fadeOut` | seconds | no | – | Audio fade-out at the clip end, seconds (0 removes). |
| `pictureFadeIn` | seconds | no | – | Picture fade-in at the clip start, seconds (0 removes): from black on a full-frame clip of a video track, from transparent on an overlay track or a boxed picture. In a list mixing picture and sound clips (a clip with its linked sound), picture fades go to the picture clips and audio fades to the sound clips, so one call fades both. |
| `pictureFadeOut` | seconds | no | – | Picture fade-out at the clip end, seconds (0 removes): to black, or to transparent (as pictureFadeIn). |
| `gain` | number | no | – | Audio gain in dB (−60…24; 0 removes). |
| `text` | string | no | – | New text of a title clip (title.add); \n starts a new line. Style, timing and position stay. |
| `fields` | object | no | – | Motion template clip (motion.add): fields to change (names from effects.catalog); the others stay. |
| `effectId` | string | no | – | An effect of the clip (effect.add) whose effectAmount changes. |
| `effectAmount` | number | no | – | New peak strength 0…1 of effectId. |
| `reset` | boolean | no | – | Clear transform, keyframes and grade first. |

Returns: the changed clips.

### `clip.speed`

**Change the speed** · MCP tool: `clip_speed` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Change a clip's speed: a constant rate (0.5 = slow motion, 2 = double), a preset (slowmo, superSlowmo 0.25×, fast, timelapse 4×, hero = normal → slow → normal, rampIn = fast → slow, rampOut = slow → fast, reverse, normal = reset), an explicit ramp of rates [{time (s into the clip's source), rate, easing}], reverse (plays backwards, ≤ 30 s, a reversed proxy is made with ffmpeg), or a freeze frame (freezeAt + freezeDuration: the clip is cut there and that frame holds). The linked sound follows: pitch kept (time-stretched) between 0.25× and 4×, muted outside, when reversed or frozen. Later clips on every track move to make room (ripple, default true). Run captions.generate again afterwards. Returns the clip(s) and the new duration.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | – | Clip to retime (its linked sound follows unless linked: false). |
| `rate` | number | no | – | Constant speed 0.1…16 (1 = normal). |
| `preset` | one of `normal`, `slowmo`, `superSlowmo`, `fast`, `timelapse`, `hero`, `rampIn`, `rampOut`, `reverse` | no | – | Ready-made speed. |
| `ramp` | array of object | no | – | Rate keyframes [{time (s from the clip's source start), rate, easing}] (a speed ramp). |
| `reverse` | boolean | no | – | Play backwards (with rate, at that speed). |
| `freezeAt` | seconds | no | – | Timeline time of a freeze frame inside the clip. |
| `freezeDuration` | seconds | no | 1 s | How long the frame holds (default 1 s). |
| `audio` | one of `pitch`, `mute` | no | pitch between 0.25× and 4×, else mute | pitch (time-stretched, pitch kept) or mute; default: pitch between 0.25× and 4×, else mute. |
| `ripple` | boolean | no | true | Move later clips (all tracks) by the length change (default true; false fails if the clip would overlap the next). |
| `linked` | boolean | no | true | Also act on the clips linked to it (picture/sound of the same take), default true. |

Returns: the clip(s) and the new duration.

## cursor

### `cursor.style`

**Cursor style** · MCP tool: `cursor_style` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Style the drawn cursor of a screen recording made without the system cursor (Registra's «Nascondi il cursore», or recording.synthesize cursor: false): the compositor redraws the macOS cursor from the logged path on the screen layer, so it follows the crop and zoom keyframes — smoothed by a critically damped spring, bigger, faded out after 2 s idle (0.3 s, back on movement), with an expanding ring on each click. Only the given fields change (reset: true goes back to the defaults first); one undo step. Takes with the cursor baked into the video store the style but cannot hide that cursor (a warning says so). Returns the style and whether it is drawn.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | boolean | no | true | Draw the cursor (default true; false hides it, ripples included). |
| `scale` | number | no | 1.5 | Size relative to the system cursor, 0.5–4 (default 1.5). |
| `smoothing` | number | no | 0.5 | Spring smoothing of the path, 0 (raw) – 1 (floaty) (default 0.5). |
| `hideWhenIdle` | boolean | no | true | Fade out after 2 s without movement or click (default true). |
| `clickRipple` | boolean | no | true | An expanding ring on each click (default true). |
| `color` | string | no | white | Ripple colour #RRGGBB (default white; "" = default). |
| `reset` | boolean | no | – | Start from the defaults instead of the current style. |
| `recordingId` | string | no | the last imported | Recording (default: the last imported). |

Returns: the style and whether it is drawn.

## edit

### `edit.autoCut`

**Automatic cut** · MCP tool: `edit_autoCut` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Build the rough cut from the chosen takes: one clip per kept range (each chosen take, the pauses longer than maxPause inside it cut out; filler words stay: transcript.deleteWords removes them) on a video track and the same ranges on an audio track, linked and frame-snapped so picture and sound cut together; 15 ms audio fades. replace: true rebuilds after takes.select. Expressed as ordinary track.add / timeline.delete / timeline.place commands, undone as one step. Returns the segments (line, take, source in/out, timeline start), track ids and duration.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `videoTrackId` | string | no | the first one, created if missing | Video track (default: the first one, created if missing). |
| `audioTrackId` | string | no | the first one, created if missing | Audio track (default: the first one, created if missing). |
| `replace` | boolean | no | false: fail if they are not empty | Remove the clips already on those tracks first (default false: fail if they are not empty). |
| `fades` | seconds | no | 0.015 | Audio micro-fade at both edges of every sound clip, seconds (default 0.015; 0 = none). |
| `maxPause` | number | no | – | Pauses longer than this inside a take are cut out, seconds: recomputes the takes' cut points (as takes.list maxPause), keeping the picks made with takes.select. |
| `keepPause` | number | no | – | Breath kept on each side of a removed pause, seconds: recomputes the cut points (as takes.list keepPause), keeping the picks. |
| `picks` | array of object | no | – | Takes to use, applied first as takes.select would: [{line, take}] (1-based, as in takes.list), so a new pick and the cut it needs are one undo step. |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | – | Only return the commands, change nothing. |

Returns: the segments (line, take, source in/out, timeline start), track ids and duration.

### `edit.autoZoom`

**Automatic zoom** · MCP tool: `edit_autoZoom` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Screen Studio-style zooms on the recording's clicks: the screen clip zooms in smoothly onto each click (zoom), holds, pans to the next click when clicks come close together, then zooms back out — crop keyframes on the screen clips, one undo step (re-running replaces them). follow: true also keeps the resting framing on the smoothed cursor (vertical reels showing a slice of a wide screen), holding still while the cursor stays inside the central safeZone of the frame. A drag (press, move, release) keeps the zoom and carries the camera along with it instead of zooming out mid-drag. Camera moves get a motion blur proportional to their speed (motionBlur). Returns the clicks with their timeline times and the zoom reached, and the drags found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zoom` | number | no | 1.8 | Magnification at a click (default 1.8; 1.3–2.5 reads well). |
| `hold` | number | no | 1.0 | Seconds held after the last click of a group (default 1.0). |
| `easeIn` | number | no | 0.45 | Seconds of the zoom-in, ending on the click (default 0.45). |
| `easeOut` | number | no | 0.6 | Seconds of the zoom-out (default 0.6). |
| `easing` | one of `smooth`, `spring`, `linear`, `easeIn`, `easeOut`, `easeInOut`, `expoOut` | no | smooth = easeInOut | Curve of the moves (default smooth = easeInOut; spring: a critically damped spring fitted to the same durations, it leaves at once and settles softly onto the click). |
| `follow` | boolean | no | false: centred | Resting framing follows the smoothed cursor (default false: centred). |
| `safeZone` | number | no | 0.6 | Follow only: central fraction of the frame the cursor may wander in before the camera moves, just enough to bring it back (default 0.6; 0 = follow every move, dense keyframes). |
| `motionBlur` | number | no | 0.5 | Blur of the camera moves, proportional to their speed, as a shutter fraction 0…1 (default 0.5; 0 = none). Written on the screen clips. |
| `drags` | boolean | no | true | Hold the zoom through drags and follow them (default true). Drags come from the session's mouse-up log (Drags.detect); older sessions without it: a click whose cursor keeps moving ≥ 0.16 s over > 1.5% of the screen diagonal. |
| `from` | seconds | no | 0 | Only clicks from this timeline time (default 0). |
| `to` | seconds | no | the end | Only clicks before this timeline time (default: the end). |
| `clear` | boolean | no | – | Remove the automatic zoom instead: the zoom keyframes and the motion blur of the screen clips (in from…to). |
| `recordingId` | string | no | the last imported | Recording (default: the last imported). |

Returns: the clicks with their timeline times and the zoom reached, and the drags found.

### `edit.beatSync`

**Cuts on the beat** · MCP tool: `edit_beatSync` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Cut or punch on the music: finds the beats of the music track (tempo + beat grid from the onsets, local DSP) and adds, every `every` beats inside [from, to), a punch-in zoom (mode punch, default every 4 beats = once a bar), a cut with alternating framing (mode cuts: the main clip is cut on the beat and every other segment is zoomed in) or a marker (mode markers). Taste: punches on downbeats of the chorus, not on every beat of the reel. Returns the tempo, the beats and what was added.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | one of `punch`, `cuts`, `markers` | no | punch | What to do on the beats (default punch). |
| `musicTrackId` | string | no | the track with role music, else the second audio track | Music track (default: the track with role music, else the second audio track). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one | Video track to cut or punch (default: the first one). |
| `every` | integer | no | punch 4, cuts 2, markers 1 | One event every n beats (default: punch 4, cuts 2, markers 1). |
| `offset` | integer | no | 0 | Skip this many beats first (default 0). |
| `from` | seconds | no | 0 | Timeline start of the range (default 0). |
| `to` | seconds | no | the end of the picture | Timeline end (default: the end of the picture). |
| `zoom` | number | no | 1.08 punch, 1.12 cuts | Punch / cut zoom (default 1.08 punch, 1.12 cuts). |
| `beats` | array of number | no | – | Use these beat times (timeline s) instead of detecting them. |

Returns: the tempo, the beats and what was added.

### `edit.punchIns`

**Punch-ins** · MCP tool: `edit_punchIns` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Hide jump cuts by alternating two framings over the clips of a video track (a base crop and a tighter punch-in), switching at every clip or only when the script line changes (by "line"). Default (no crops given): face-aware crops per shot from the face track (run faces.track first) — every detected face kept in frame (a child in the arms too), room above the hair, never a head cut, static when one crop holds the shot, else smoothed and speed-limited; zoom sets how tight base and punch are. preset "wesites-selfie" = the fixed crops approved on the WeSites 1080×1920 selfie take (2026-10-26) (base [864,1536,152,384], punch [760,1351,204,487]); base/punch = your own fixed crops; mode "face" = fixed sizes centred on the main face. Expressed as clip.set commands, one undo step. Returns each clip's framing, crop, whether every head fits, and the face count.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | array of number | no | – | Fixed base crop [w, h, x, y] in source pixels (face mode: only w, h are used). |
| `punch` | array of number | no | – | Fixed punch-in crop [w, h, x, y] (face mode: only w, h are used). |
| `preset` | one of `wesites-selfie` | no | – | Named fixed crops (wesites-selfie: the approved WeSites selfie take). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one | Video track (default: the first one). |
| `mode` | one of `auto`, `alternate`, `face` | no | without crops | auto (default without crops): face-aware crops; alternate: the fixed crops; face: fixed sizes centred on the main face. |
| `zoom` | array of number | no | [0.8, 0.7] | auto: crop height of base and punch as fractions of the largest crop (default [0.8, 0.7]); grown when the heads need it. |
| `headroom` | number | no | 0.05 | auto: room above the hair, fraction of the crop height (default 0.05). |
| `by` | one of `clip`, `line` | no | – | Switch framing at every clip (default) or only when the script line changes (needs takes). |
| `startWith` | one of `base`, `punch` | no | base | Framing of the first clip (default base). |
| `pad` | number | no | 0.25 | Face mode: room added above the face box, fraction of its height (default 0.25). |
| `smooth` | number | no | 0.5 face, 0.6 auto | Face/auto mode: moving-average window on the crop position, seconds (default 0.5 face, 0.6 auto). |

Returns: each clip's framing, crop, whether every head fits, and the face count.

## effect

### `effect.add`

**Add an effect** · MCP tool: `effect_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Add a keyframable Core Image effect to a clip over a window (timeline times): lut (.cube file), blur, glow, vignette, sharpen, punchZoom (zoom bump on a beat, default 1.12×), shake (hand-held), flash (the frame washes to white/colour), glitch (RGB split + jittering blocks; a few frames on a hard cut, never a whole sentence), chromaKey (green/blue screen on an overlay clip: color, tolerance, spill). Strength = amount with attack/release ramps, or explicit keyframes [{time, value, easing}]. Use sparingly: one punch or flash on a strong beat, not on every line. Returns the effect id and the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `lut`, `blur`, `glow`, `vignette`, `sharpen`, `punchZoom`, `shake`, `flash`, `glitch`, `chromaKey` | yes | – | Effect. |
| `clipId` | string | no | – | Clip (or trackId + at). |
| `trackId` | string | no | – | Track whose clip at `at` (or `start`) gets the effect. |
| `at` | seconds | no | – | Timeline time used with trackId to find the clip. |
| `start` | seconds | no | the clip start | Timeline start of the effect (default: the clip start). |
| `end` | seconds | no | the clip end | Timeline end (default: the clip end). |
| `amount` | number | no | 1 | Peak strength 0…1 (default 1; flash 0.8). |
| `attack` | number | no | 0.08 | Ramp in, seconds (punchZoom default 0.08). |
| `release` | number | no | 0.25 | Ramp out, seconds (punchZoom default 0.25). |
| `easing` | one of `linear`, `easeIn`, `easeOut`, `easeInOut`, `expoOut`, `backOut`, `hold`, `spring` | no | easeOut | Ramp curve (default easeOut). |
| `keyframes` | array of object | no | – | Strength curve [{time (timeline s), value, easing}] instead of amount/attack/release. |
| `radius` | number | no | – | blur/glow/sharpen radius px at 1080 wide; vignette size (0…1). |
| `zoom` | number | no | 1.12 | punchZoom peak scale (default 1.12). |
| `path` | string | no | – | lut: the .cube file. |
| `color` | string | no | #FFFFFF | flash colour (default #FFFFFF); chromaKey key colour (default #00FF00). |
| `frequency` | number | no | 7 | shake Hz (default 7); glitch pattern changes per second (default 12). |
| `tolerance` | number | no | 0.4 | chromaKey: width of the keyed colour range 0…1 (default 0.4). |
| `spill` | number | no | 0.5 | chromaKey: key-colour fringe removed from the kept pixels 0…1 (default 0.5). |

Returns: the effect id and the clip.

## effects

### `effects.catalog`

**Read the effects catalogue** · MCP tool: `effects_catalog` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Everything the user can add from the app's Graphics panel, and the way to recommend it: looks (filters), adjustments, zooms, FX, text and callouts, stickers, transitions, speed, logo motions, one-click styles and motion templates (animated cards, checklists, counters, carousels, device frames, charts… category templates). Each item has an English description (what it looks like), useWhen (when to propose it), avoid (when not to), its fields with example values, what it needs (a clip, a moment, or the whole picture) and the ordinary command it runs. Read it before dressing a reel: pick 1–3 items that fit a line, tell the user why, show one with effects.preview on request, then apply it. With item (+ clipId/start/end/intensity/fields) it also returns the exact command and params to run. brief: true lists only id, label and description. Returns the items.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | one of `filters`, `adjust`, `zoom`, `motion`, `text`, `stickers`, `transitions`, `speed`, `logo`, `captions`, `layouts`, `styles`, `templates` | no | – | Only this category. |
| `item` | string | no | – | One item id: also resolve its command. |
| `clipId` | string | no | – | Target clip for item. |
| `start` | seconds | no | the clip start, else 0 | Target moment for item (default: the clip start, else 0). |
| `end` | seconds | no | – | Target range end for item. |
| `intensity` | number | no | 0.5 | 0…1 (default 0.5). |
| `fields` | object | no | – | Field values for item (names from its fields); they override the resolved params. |
| `brief` | boolean | no | – | Only id, category, label and description per item (a quick overview). |

Returns: the items.

### `effects.check`

**Check the effects** · MCP tool: `effects_check` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Test helper: verify the effects of the timeline. For every clip effect, sticker, callout, title, transition and look it renders the frame where it is strongest with and without it (quarter size, same compositor) and measures the difference (visible = a clear difference over at least 0.2 % of the frame); renders a look at intensity 0 against no look (must be identical); checks sticker/callout boxes against the caption band; checks each retimed clip's duration against its speed; with path (a render), measures the A/V offset of retimed clips with stretched sound (energy envelopes, must be under one frame). Returns per-item results and pass.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | – | Rendered mp4: also check A/V sync of the retimed clips. |
| `minDiff` | number | no | 8 | Mean difference (0…255) over the changed pixels for an effect to count as visible (default 8). |

Returns: per-item results and pass.

### `effects.preview`

**Effect preview** · MCP tool: `effects_preview` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Show the user what a catalog item would look like before applying it ("show me that effect"): applies the item (effects.catalog id, with optional field values) to a throwaway copy of the project and renders it with the export compositor at a moment — one still at the moment it shows best, or `frames` (2–12) evenly over its animation as one contact sheet. The edit and the undo history are not touched. Returns the image(s) inline, their paths, the command and params that would apply it, and the time window.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | string | yes | – | Catalog item id (effects.catalog). |
| `fields` | object | no | – | Field values (names from the item's fields), e.g. {"title": "…", "rows": ["…"]}. |
| `at` | seconds | no | one third into the timeline | Timeline moment to apply it at (default: one third into the timeline). |
| `clipId` | string | no | the clip under `at` | Target clip (items that need a clip; default: the clip under `at`). |
| `intensity` | number | no | 0.5 | 0…1 (default 0.5). |
| `frames` | integer | no | – | 1 = one still (default); 2–12 = a contact sheet across the item's animation. |
| `captions` | boolean | no | true | Draw the captions too (default true). |
| `preset` | one of `9:16`, `4:5`, `1:1`, `16:9` | no | the project size | 9:16 (1080×1920), 4:5 (1080×1350, feed portrait), 1:1 (1080×1080) or 16:9 (1920×1080); another aspect than the project's reframes every clip by crop (default: the project size). |

Returns: the image(s) inline, their paths, the command and params that would apply it, and the time window.

### `export.render`

**Export the video** · MCP tool: `export_render` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Render the final video: the timeline to an mp4 with the same compositor frame.render uses (crops/keyframes/grade, captions drawn natively); H.264 High yuv420p 30 fps, faststart, AAC 48 kHz 192 kb/s; preset "9:16" for a reel. The sound is the mix of the unmuted audio tracks through a limiter. It runs rules.check first and refuses while a rule of the project's kind fails, with the list and the fixes (rules.fix {all: true} applies the safe ones). Returns frames, duration, the measured loudness (expect −15 ±0.5 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.5), the rule check and warnings (e.g. stale captions).

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `preset` | one of `9:16`, `4:5`, `1:1`, `16:9` | no | the project size | 9:16 (1080×1920), 4:5 (1080×1350, feed portrait), 1:1 (1080×1080) or 16:9 (1920×1080); another aspect than the project's reframes every clip by crop (default: the project size). |
| `captions` | boolean | no | true | Draw the caption track (default true). |
| `bitrate` | number | no | 14 | Video bit rate, Mb/s (default 14). |
| `ceiling` | number | no | -1.5 | True-peak ceiling of the mix, dBTP (default -1.5). |
| `loudness` | number | no | no correction (the voice is already at -15 | Integrated loudness target of the final mix, LUFS (e.g. -15 once music and SFX are added): the mix is measured and re-made with one static gain before the limiter. Default: no correction (the voice is already at -15). |
| `exportAnyway` | boolean | no | – | Export although an editing rule fails. Only when the user said to export anyway, after being told what fails; never on your own. |

Returns: frames, duration, the measured loudness (expect −15 ±0.5 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.5), the rule check and warnings (e.g. stale captions).

### `generate.run`

Generate a still, a clip, a music bed or a voice-over (kind voice: the owner's cloned voice, VoxCPM2, see voice.list) and add it to the media bin (asset with provider, model, prompt, seed, cost, created). Then place it: overlay.add {path, fullFrame: true} for B-roll, audio.addMusic {path} for music, timeline.place for a voice-over. Higgsfield (paid) needs approval (token from the human via generate.approve) and draws on the 2-call budget. | `size` | array of integer | no | 720×1280 still, 464×832 clip | [width, height] in pixels (ComfyUI: multiples of 16; default 720×1280 still, 464×832 clip). Higgsfield uses it for the aspect ratio. |
| `seed` | integer | no | derived from the prompt, so the same request is cached | Seed (default: derived from the prompt, so the same request is cached). |
| `options` | object | no | – | Provider flags as strings, e.g. {"resolution": "480p", "generate_audio": "false"} (Higgsfield) or {"bpm": "100"} (ACE-Step). Voice: {"voice": "ada", "language": "fr", "tone": "neutral"} (voice.list shows them; voice and language may be left out when there is only one). |

### `graphics.checkBehindSubject`

Check a behindSubject title/overlay: at sample times it renders the frame with the layer, without it, and with it in front, then reads the person matte where the layer has pixels. ## keys

### `keys.overlay`

**Keys pressed in the video** · MCP tool: `keys_overlay` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Show the keyboard shortcuts pressed during a screen recording as on-screen key badges (⇧⌘K, ⌘Z ×3) — from the keystrokes Regista logged while recording. Only shortcuts (⌘/⌃/⌥ combinations, F-keys) by default; allKeys also shows special keys (↩ ⎋ ⇥ arrows) and typing, each run of typed characters collapsed into one badge of the text. Badges sit bottom-centre (above the caption band in a 9:16 reel) on a 'Tasti' overlay track, styled from the brand kit (ink chip, paper text, the kit's bold face), timed through the screen clips: cuts, trims and speed changes are followed and keys of cut-out moments are dropped. Re-running replaces the badges (one undo step); clear: true removes them. Returns the badges with their timeline times.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allKeys` | boolean | no | false: shortcuts only | Also special keys and typing (runs of typed characters collapsed into one badge); default false: shortcuts only. |
| `position` | one of `bottom`, `top` | no | bottom-centre, above the caption band in a 9:16 reel | bottom (default: bottom-centre, above the caption band in a 9:16 reel) or top. |
| `hold` | number | no | 1.0 | Seconds a badge stays after its last key (default 1.0). |
| `size` | number | no | ~3.8% of the frame's shorter side | Font size, px per 1080 of the output width (default: ~3.8% of the frame's shorter side). |
| `from` | seconds | no | 0 | Only keys from this timeline time (default 0). |
| `to` | seconds | no | the end | Only keys before this timeline time (default: the end). |
| `clear` | boolean | no | – | Remove the key badges (and their track) instead. |
| `recordingId` | string | no | the last imported | Recording (default: the last imported). |

Returns: the badges with their timeline times.

## layout

### `layout.apply`

**Change the layout** · MCP tool: `layout_apply` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Put the face where a layout preset says on a time range of a screen recording (default: the whole recording): cuts the screen, camera and mic clips at the range edges and writes placement, crop around the face (faces.track on the camera makes it exact), mask and border on them — ordinary clip properties, editable with clip.set/clip.keyframe. Replaces the boxes moved by hand (clip.place) in the range. Switching mid-video: call it again on a later range; a move between two layouts of the same shape glides (transition seconds), a new shape pops in. cutout needs matte.track {assetId: <camera>} over the range. screen and bubble take a styled frame (frame: true or background/gradient/padding/radius/shadow): the whole screen padded on a gradient, colour or image background with rounded corners and a soft shadow — the project's backdrop, default from the brand kit. Returns the camera clips written and the boxes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset` | one of `bubble`, `split`, `stack`, `face`, `cutout`, `screen` | yes | – | bubble, split, stack, face, cutout or screen (layout.presets). |
| `from` | seconds | no | the start of the recording | Timeline start (default: the start of the recording). |
| `to` | seconds | no | the end of the recording | Timeline end (default: the end of the recording). |
| `transition` | number | no | 0.35 | Seconds of the move into this layout at `from` (default 0.35; 0 = a hard cut). |
| `recordingId` | string | no | the last imported | Recording (default: the last imported). |
| `corner` | one of `topLeft`, `topRight`, `bottomLeft`, `bottomRight` | no | bottomRight | bubble: corner of the face (default bottomRight); cutout: bottomLeft or bottomRight. |
| `shape` | one of `circle`, `rounded` | no | – | bubble: circle (default) or rounded (rounded square). |
| `size` | one of `S`, `M`, `L` | no | – | bubble / cutout: S, M (default) or L. |
| `side` | one of `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` | no | – | split: face on the right (default) or left; stack: face at the bottom (default) or top. |
| `frame` | boolean | no | – | screen / bubble: a styled frame — the whole screen (never cropped) on a background with padding, rounded corners and a soft shadow. Implied by any of the frame options below; false removes it. |
| `background` | string | no | when a kit is applied, else graphite | Frame background: a built-in gradient (graphite, aurum, dusk, lagoon, mist, sand; layout.presets describes them), brand (the applied kit's colours: the default when a kit is applied, else graphite), a colour #RRGGBB, or an image file (aspect fill). |
| `gradient` | array of string | no | – | Frame background: a custom gradient of 2–3 colours #RRGGBB (instead of background). |
| `gradientKind` | one of `linear`, `radial` | no | – | Custom gradient: linear (default) or radial (from the centre). |
| `angle` | number | no | – | Linear gradient direction, degrees: 0 towards the top, 90 towards the right, 180 towards the bottom (default). |
| `padding` | number | no | 0.06 | Frame: space around the screen, fraction of the frame's shorter side (default 0.06; 0–0.3). |
| `radius` | number | no | 0.016 | Frame: screen corner radius, fraction of the frame's shorter side (default 0.016; 0 = square corners). |
| `shadow` | number | no | 0.5 | Frame: opacity of the soft shadow under the screen, 0–1 (default 0.5; 0 = none). |

Returns: the camera clips written and the boxes.

### `layout.speaker`

**Speaker layout** · MCP tool: `layout_speaker` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Frame the speaker (any project, not only screen recordings) on a time range: letterbox-headline (9:16: black top band with a persistent headline, the 16:9 picture in the middle, the bottom band empty for Instagram's buttons — captions land under the picture), split-card (the speaker in a rounded card on one side, a free area on the other for a graphic; light canvas), pip-bubble (the speaker in a circle in a corner over a full-frame graphic or B-roll: brollAssetId fills the frame under it), inset-frame (the whole shot shrinks into a styled card on a dark backdrop — frame neon (glow + corner brackets + PREVIEW chip, brand accent), glass or plain; position center, topLeft or left of a panel; animates in from full frame and back out), full (removes the layout). Cuts the main video at the range edges and writes ordinary clip properties (box placement, crop around the face — faces.track makes it exact —, mask), so clip.set and history.undo work. A pip-bubble without B-roll over a face-tracked speaker goes to the first corner that leaves the face free (a corner given is kept, with a warning when it covers the face). Returns the clips written, the speaker box, the free area for a graphic, the bubble's corner, faceCheck (whether the corner was checked against a face, or why not) and warnings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset` | one of `letterbox-headline`, `split-card`, `pip-bubble`, `inset-frame`, `full` | yes | – | letterbox-headline, split-card, pip-bubble, inset-frame or full. |
| `from` | seconds | no | 0 | Timeline start (default 0). |
| `to` | seconds | no | the end of the speaker track | Timeline end (default: the end of the speaker track). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first video track with clips | The speaker's video track (default: the first video track with clips). |
| `headline` | string | no | – | letterbox-headline: the text of the top band (sentence case, ≤ 6 words reads best). |
| `side` | one of `left`, `right` | no | left | split-card: side of the card (default left). |
| `corner` | one of `topLeft`, `topRight`, `bottomLeft`, `bottomRight` | no | bottomRight, kept clear of the Instagram rail and the caption band | pip-bubble: corner (default bottomRight, kept clear of the Instagram rail and the caption band; without B-roll and over a face-tracked speaker, the first corner of bottomRight, bottomLeft, topRight, topLeft that leaves the face free). A corner given is kept, with a warning when the bubble covers the face. |
| `size` | one of `S`, `M`, `L` | no | M | pip-bubble: S, M or L (default M). |
| `brollAssetId` | string | no | – | pip-bubble: a video or image asset filling the frame under the bubble over the range. |
| `brollIn` | seconds | no | 0 | pip-bubble: start inside the B-roll (default 0). |
| `position` | one of `center`, `topLeft`, `left` | no | – | inset-frame: center (default), topLeft or left (a panel on the right). |
| `frame` | one of `neon`, `glass`, `plain` | no | – | inset-frame: neon (default), glass or plain. |

| `accent` | string | no | the kit's highlight, else #FF7A1A | Glow / accent colour (#RRGGBB or a brand role; default the kit's highlight, else #FF7A1A). |
| `background` | string | no | – | Frame background around the box (#RRGGBB or a brand role; defaults per preset). |

Returns: the clips written, the speaker box, the free area for a graphic, the bubble's corner, faceCheck (whether the corner was checked against a face, or why not) and warnings.

## logo

### `logo.add`

**Add the logo** · MCP tool: `logo_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Put the brand logo over the video: the applied kit's logo (or kit / path), at the kit's placement — a corner inside the Instagram safe area, never in the caption band — sized in px at 1080 wide, faded in and out. By default it spans the whole timeline (a watermark) — unless the project's rules want the logo only at the end (logo-end, on in the default rules): then it goes in the closing 2 s of the video and the result's timing says so; pass start/duration for any other time (rules.check then judges it). clipId moves a logo already placed instead (the logo-end fix): to the closing seconds, or to start/end, keeping its look. brandkit.apply swaps it when the kit changes. Returns the clip, its box and warnings.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `end` | seconds | no | – | Timeline end instead of duration. |
| `kit` | string | no | the applied kit | Kit whose logo to use (default: the applied kit). |
| `path` | string | no | – | A logo file instead (.svg or .png). |
| `variant` | one of `onDark`, `onLight`, `mark` | no | – | onDark (default), onLight or mark. |

| `animation` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `bounce`, `none`, `spin`, `orbit`, `pulse`, `sting` | no | the kit's, else fade | Entrance (exit fades) — fade, pop, slideUp, slideDown, none — or a logo motion: spin, orbit (slow drift), pulse (breathing), sting (pop-in hit, for a closing card). Default: the kit's, else fade. |
| `trackId` | string | no | the Logo track, created if needed | Track (default: the Logo track, created if needed). |
| `replace` | boolean | no | – | Remove the logo clips already on the timeline first (one undo step: move or resize the logo). |

**Animate the logo** · MCP tool: `logo_animate` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

## look

### `look.apply`

**Apply a look** · MCP tool: `look_apply` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Apply a colour look (filter) with an intensity, to clips or — with no clip — to the whole picture (video, inserts and layout boxes; titles, stickers, logos keep their colours). Looks: golden (Dorato), frost (Brina), film (Pellicola), graphite (Grafite, b&w), ink (Inchiostro, hard b&w), vivid (Vivido), velvet (Velluto), riviera (Riviera, teal & orange), archive (Archivio), matte (Opaco), sunset (Tramonto), fjord (Fiordo), night (Notte), airy (Luce); none removes it. Intensity 0 draws exactly the original. Taste: one look for the whole reel, 40–70 %. Returns the grade.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `look` | one of `golden`, `frost`, `film`, `graphite`, `ink`, `vivid`, `velvet`, `riviera`, `archive`, `matte`, `sunset`, `fjord`, `night`, `airy`, `none` | yes | – | Look id (look.list), or none. |
| `amount` | number | no | 1 | Intensity 0…1 (default 1; 0.5 is often enough). |
| `clipId` | string | no | the whole picture | Clip (default: the whole picture). |
| `clipIds` | array of string | no | – | Several clips. |

Returns: the grade.
