List the colour looks (filters) for look.apply — id, Italian name, what it does — and the Photos-style adjustments for adjust.set with their ranges. Returns looks and adjustments.

No parameters.

Returns: looks and adjustments.

## matte

### `matte.track`

**Cut out the person** · MCP tool: `matte_track` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Track the speaker's person matte (Apple Vision person segmentation, quality balanced, on-device, any tier) on the camera frames the timeline shows between from and to (default the whole timeline), smoothed over neighbouring frames and cached as a sidecar (frames already tracked are skipped). Needed for behindSubject: true on title.add / overlay.add (text behind the person: the hook title, once per reel). Returns frames tracked, coverage and timing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | no | the asset of the bottom video track | Camera asset (default: the asset of the bottom video track). |
| `from` | seconds | no | 0 | Timeline start (default 0). |
| `to` | seconds | no | the end of the timeline | Timeline end (default: the end of the timeline). |

Returns: frames tracked, coverage and timing.

## media

### `media.checkOverlay`

**Check an overlay** · MCP tool: `media_checkOverlay` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Verify that overlay clips (e.g. full-frame inserts) are visible exactly in their windows in a rendered file: frames decoded from the render are compared (luma PSNR) with the same timeline drawn without those clips, at each clip's first and last frame (must differ) and at the frame before and after (must match). Returns per-clip PSNRs and pass.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Rendered video. |
| `trackId` | string | yes | – | The overlay track to check. |
| `clipIds` | array of string | no | all | Only these clips of the track (default: all). |
| `differ` | number | no | 25 | Inside the window the PSNR must be below this, dB (default 25). |
| `match` | number | no | 30 | Outside it must be above this, dB (default 30). |

Returns: per-clip PSNRs and pass.

### `media.checkPlacement`

**Check a placement** · MCP tool: `media_checkPlacement` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Verify where a caption chunk, title, sticker, logo or overlay really is in an exported mp4: the frame decoded from the file is compared with the same frame rendered without that element; the box of the pixels that differ is where the element was drawn. Compared with the render plan's box (frame.elements) — pass when the centres agree within the tolerance. Returns the found box, the planned box and the error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Rendered video (export.render output, project size). |
| `clipId` | string | no | – | A title, sticker, logo or overlay clip. |
| `chunk` | integer | no | – | A caption chunk (instead of clipId). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one with captions | Caption track (default: the first one with captions). |
| `time` | seconds | no | a chunk's last frame, when every word shows | Frame to check (default: a chunk's last frame, when every word shows; a clip's middle). |
| `tolerance` | number | no | 4 | Pixels of centre error still passing (default 4). |

Returns: the found box, the planned box and the error.

### `media.checkSync`

**Check the sync** · MCP tool: `media_checkSync` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Verify A/V sync of an exported mp4: its sound cross-correlated with the camera sound of the clips laid out on the timeline, over windows in the middle of the longest clips. Positive lag = sound late; pass = under one frame. Returns lag (ms, frames) and correlation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Rendered video. |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first audio track | Audio track whose clips define the layout (default: the first audio track). |
| `windows` | integer | no | 8 | Number of 2 s windows (default 8). |

Returns: lag (ms, frames) and correlation.

### `media.compare`

**Compare two files** · MCP tool: `media_compare` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Test helper: compare a render with a reference video frame by frame (ffmpeg SSIM and PSNR on sampled frames). align "time" compares the same timestamps; align "source" maps each sampled frame of the candidate (this project's video track) and of the reference (its segments.json) to the source frame it shows and compares frames showing the same source frame, away from cuts in both. Returns SSIM/PSNR statistics.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `candidate` | string | yes | – | The render to judge. |
| `reference` | string | yes | – | The reference video. |
| `samples` | integer | no | 30 | Number of sampled frames (default 30). |
| `times` | array of number | no | – | Candidate times to compare instead of evenly spaced samples. |
| `align` | one of `time`, `source` | no | – | time (default) or source (needs referenceSegments). |
| `referenceSegments` | string | no | – | The reference's segments.json (source in/out per segment, concatenated at 30 fps). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first video track | Candidate video track for align source (default: the first video track). |
| `cutMargin` | integer | no | 5 | align source: frames kept away from every cut (default 5). |

Returns: SSIM/PSNR statistics.

### `media.extractAudio`

**Extract the audio** · MCP tool: `media_extractAudio` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Step 1 of the analysis: extract an asset's audio — a 16 kHz mono wav (speech engines) and a 48 kHz mono working wav (voice chain), sample-aligned with the video, into the project's media folder. Run it right after media.import. Returns the wav paths.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes | – | Asset with an audio track. |
| `force` | boolean | no | false | Extract again even if the files exist (default false). |

Returns: the wav paths.

### `media.import`

**Import a file** · MCP tool: `media_import` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Add a media file (from media.list) to the project before using it: reads duration, fps, size, rotation and audio with ffprobe; the file is never modified. A teleprompter recording's live take markers (<name>.takes.json next to it) come along for takes.list. A picture (PNG, JPEG, HEIC, WebP, SVG rasterized) becomes a still image asset, placed as an overlay (overlay.add) or on a track (timeline.place: 5 s by default). Importing the same path twice returns the existing asset. Returns the asset (its id, e.g. a1, is what the other tools take).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Absolute path of the video, audio or image file (~ is expanded). |
| `name` | string | no | file name | Display name (default: file name). |

Returns: the asset (its id, e.g. a1, is what the other tools take).

### `media.list`

**List files** · MCP tool: `media_list` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Use this first to find footage, scripts and earlier projects when you have no file tools: lists the media folders Regista may read (the roots) and the video, audio, image, text (.md/.txt/.srt/.json), project (.regista) and Shotcut (.mlt) files in them, with size and date. A screen recording made in Regista is a folder with a session.json (pass the folder to recording.import). Returns roots (and whether each exists), projectsDirectory (pass it to project.new as directory), exportsDirectory (where export.render / export.srt files go), outputDirectory (their parent, for anything else) and files [{path, kind, bytes, modified}]; pass a path to media.import, script.set, text.read or project.open.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | every root | Only this folder (absolute, or relative to a root); default: every root. |
| `kinds` | array of one of `audio`, `image`, `project`, `shotcut`, `text`, `video` | no | all | Only these kinds (default: all). |
| `depth` | integer | no | 3 | How many folder levels to descend (default 3). |

Returns: roots (and whether each exists), projectsDirectory (pass it to project.new as directory), exportsDirectory (where export.render / export.srt files go), outputDirectory (their parent, for anything else) and files [{path, kind, bytes, modified}]; pass a path to media.import, script.set, text.read or project.open.

Measure EBU R128 loudness (integrated LUFS, true peak dBTP, LRA) of an asset's audio, or of a track as it plays (its clips one after the other). Mono is measured as dual-mono stereo, like the export. Returns the measurement.

Test helper: write a synthetic talking head (1080×1920 30 fps H.264: a wall, a speaker silhouette that sways and nods) with its exact person matte, import it and attach the matte (as matte.track would), so behind-the-speaker graphics can be tested without footage or Vision; optionally its exact face track (as faces.track would) and spoken words (as transcript.run would). ## meters

### `meters.add`

**Add a meter** · MCP tool: `meters_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Stereo L/R level meters (segmented bars, green → yellow → accent at the top, a falling peak-hold tick) driven by the real sound of the edit: the audio tracks are mixed and measured every 1/30 s (RMS and peak, −48…0 dBFS). Default placement: one pair on each side of the speaker's card when a layout box is on screen (layout.speaker inset-frame), else at the frame's left and right margins mid-height. Use it on a sound beat (music, an effect, 'listen to this'), a few seconds, not the whole reel. Returns the clip and the loudest moment.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | seconds | no | 0 | Timeline start (default 0). |
| `end` | seconds | no | start + 6 s, at most the end of the picture | Timeline end (default start + 6 s, at most the end of the picture). |
| `rect` | array of number | no | beside the speaker's card | [x, y, w, h] px on a 1080×1920 frame: the left pair at x, the right pair at x + w (default: beside the speaker's card). |
| `color` | string | no | the kit's highlight, else #FF7A1A | Top segments (#RRGGBB or a brand role; default the kit's highlight, else #FF7A1A). |
| `trackId` | string | no | a free one | Overlay track (default: a free one). |

Returns: the clip and the loudest moment.

## motion

### `motion.add`

**Add an animation** · MCP tool: `motion_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Add a motion template — an animated, branded graphic drawn by the compositor: an orbit carousel of photos around the speaker, an iOS-style checklist whose ticks land on the words, a counter or clock, a swing tag, scrolling marquee rows, the shot shrinking into a phone frame, floating cards behind the speaker, a HUD viewfinder, animated charts… effects.catalog {category: "templates"} lists every template with its fields (types, example values), description, useWhen and avoid; effects.preview shows one before adding it. Colours and fonts come from the applied brand kit (fields accept #RRGGBB or colour roles: ink, paper, primary, accent, highlight). Templates that go behind the person (layering behind/split) need matte.track over their window. sync: true times a list field (e.g. checklist rows) to the transcript: each entry lands when its first word is spoken. Without band or position, over a face-tracked picture (faces.track), it takes the first place the template allows that leaves the face free for its whole time; a place given is kept, with a warning when it covers the face. Returns the clip, the fields used, the place and faceCheck (whether the place was checked against a face, or why not) and warnings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes | – | Template id (effects.catalog category templates: orbit-carousel, checklist, counter, …). |
| `start` | seconds | yes | – | Timeline start (land it on the word). |
| `duration` | seconds | no | the template's | Seconds on screen (default: the template's). Left out, the graphic ends with the main video at the latest: shortened, or started earlier to keep 1 s (the result's timing says so). |
| `end` | seconds | no | – | Timeline end instead of duration. |
| `fields` | object | no | – | Template fields (names from effects.catalog; omitted ones keep their example/default). |
| `band` | one of `top`, `middle`, `lower` | no | – | Vertical band for templates that sit in one (top y 110–640, middle, lower). Without band and position, a template over a face-tracked picture takes the first of its places (its band, then the others; or its point, then the point mirrored) that leaves the face free. |
| `position` | array of number | no | – | Centre [x, y] on a 1080×1920 frame (overrides band). Kept even over a face (the result warns). |
| `sync` | boolean | no | – | Time the template's list entries to the transcript words (checklist ticks, script lines). |
| `behind` | boolean | no | – | Draw the whole template behind the speaker (needs matte.track), e.g. a kicker headline the head passes in front of. |
| `trackId` | string | no | a free one | Overlay track (default: a free one). |

Returns: the clip, the fields used, the place and faceCheck (whether the place was checked against a face, or why not) and warnings.

## overlay

### `overlay.add`

**Add an image on top** · MCP tool: `overlay_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Put a picture over the video: a still (PNG/JPG, SVG rasterized), a PNG sequence with alpha (folder or %04d pattern: Blender, HyperFrames), an alpha video (ProRes 4444 / HEVC-alpha / VP9-alpha, decoded to RGBA frames) or a full-frame insert (fullFrame: true, e.g. an AI B-roll shot that replaces the picture for a moment). Imports the file, places it on an overlay track (one is created; overlays sit under titles), with position (band / position / top), scale, opacity, blend mode and entrance/exit animation presets. Captions are always drawn on top. Returns the clip, its asset and its box with layout warnings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Image, SVG, folder of numbered PNGs, %04d pattern, or video. |
| `start` | seconds | yes | – | Timeline start. |
| `duration` | seconds | no | the media length | Seconds on screen (default: the media length; stills 3 s). Left out, the graphic ends with the main video at the latest: shortened, or started earlier to keep 1 s (the result's timing says so). |
| `end` | seconds | no | – | Timeline end instead of duration. |
| `sourceIn` | seconds | no | 0 | Start inside a video/sequence (default 0). |
| `fullFrame` | boolean | no | – | Fill the whole frame (cropped to 9:16) instead of keeping the native size: inserts. |
| `fit` | one of `native`, `contain`, `fill` | no | – | native (own pixel size at 1080 wide), contain (whole picture fitted in the frame) or fill (= fullFrame). |
| `blend` | one of `normal`, `screen`, `multiply` | no | – | normal (default), screen (light leaks, glows on black), multiply (paper textures). |
| `alpha` | boolean | no | – | Force (true) or skip (false) alpha decoding of a video; detected from the pixel format by default. |
| `svgWidth` | integer | no | 1080 | Raster width of an SVG, px (default 1080). |
| `trackId` | string | no | a free overlay track, created if needed | Overlay track to use (default: a free overlay track, created if needed). |
| `behindSubject` | boolean | no | – | Draw it behind the speaker (between the background and the person; needs matte.track over its window). |
| `band` | one of `top`, `middle`, `lower` | no | for titles and cards | Vertical band of a 9:16 reel: top (y 110–640, the default for titles and cards), middle, lower (980–1200, just above the captions). The caption band 1230–1460 is reserved. |
| `position` | array of number | no | – | Centre [x, y] in pixels of a 1080×1920 frame (overrides band). |
| `top` | number | no | – | Top edge, pixels of a 1080×1920 frame (instead of a centre). |
| `scale` | number | no | – | Size factor (1 = native size). |
| `opacity` | number | no | 1 | 0…1 (default 1). |
| `rotation` | number | no | – | Degrees clockwise. |
| `animIn` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | – | Entrance: pop (scale with overshoot), slideUp, slideDown, fade, kenBurns (slow push over the whole clip), none. |
| `animOut` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | same as animIn | Exit (default: same as animIn; kenBurns has none). |
| `inDuration` | number | no | 0.35 | Entrance seconds (default 0.35; fade 0.25). |
| `outDuration` | number | no | 0.25 | Exit seconds (default 0.25). |

Returns: the clip, its asset and its box with layout warnings.

Headless it replaces the open project and clears undo. Returns the project summary (as project.state).

## recipe

### `recipe.get`

**Read a recipe** · MCP tool: `recipe_get` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Read this before making any video: the step-by-step recipe and the house rules for a kind of video — talking-head-reel (a person speaking to camera), screen-tutorial (a screen recording made in Regista, with or without the face), voice-over-video (no one on camera: the user's cloned voice over footage, stills and graphics), reel-graphics (titles, cards, sound effects and music on top of an edit). Without name, lists the recipes with what each is for: call it first and pick. The text ends with the editing rules of that kind of video (the user's rule sheets: they always hold, and export.render refuses while one of their checks fails). Returns {name, title, text, kind}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | one of `talking-head-reel`, `screen-tutorial`, `voice-over-video`, `reel-graphics` | no | – | Recipe: talking-head-reel, screen-tutorial, voice-over-video, reel-graphics. |
| `language` | one of `it`, `en`, `fr`, `pt` | no | sheets read (it, en, fr, pt | Language of the default sheets read (it, en, fr, pt; default: the app's interface language). A sheet the user wrote is the same in every language. |

Returns: {name, title, text, kind}.

## recording

### `recording.check`

**Check the recording** · MCP tool: `recording_check` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Check an exported screen-recording edit: sync (the session's slates: the camera flash frame, the screen flash frame and the mic beep found in the mp4 — camera↔mic and screen↔camera must be within one frame and on the expected frames), faces (Apple Vision on the export: the face inside the camera box the layout says, near its expected spot), zoom (at each click the export matches the zoomed render, not the unzoomed one) and cutout (around the person the screen shows through, the person covers it). Returns each check with numbers and pass.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | The exported mp4. |
| `checks` | array of one of `sync`, `faces`, `zoom`, `cutout` | no | all that apply | Which checks (default: all that apply). |
| `recordingId` | string | no | the last imported | Recording (default: the last imported). |

Returns: each check with numbers and pass.

### `recording.import`

**Import the recording** · MCP tool: `recording_import` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Turn a screen recording session (the folder Regista's Registra workspace or recording.synthesize writes: session.json + screen.mov, camera.mov, mic.wav) into a timeline: screen on a video track (Schermo), camera above it (Camera), mic on an audio track, all on the session's common clock (sub-frame offsets kept exactly) and linked, then the layout chosen at recording time (or `layout`) applied, including the switches made while recording. Camera and mic are optional: a screen-only take (no camera.mov) gets the `screen` layout. A take recorded without the system cursor (session cursorInVideo false) gets the cursor drawn by the compositor from the logged path (cursor.style). Returns the recording id, assets, tracks, the common window and the per-source offsets.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | session.json, or the session folder. |
| `layout` | one of `bubble`, `split`, `stack`, `face`, `cutout`, `screen` | no | the one chosen when recording, else bubble | Layout over the whole recording (default: the one chosen when recording, else bubble). |
| `start` | seconds | no | the end of the timeline, 0 when empty | Timeline time where the recording starts (default: the end of the timeline, 0 when empty). |
| `faces` | boolean | no | false: a centred upper framing | Face-track the camera first (Apple Vision, every frame: ~1 s per 10 s of video) so the layouts frame the face (default false: a centred upper framing). |
| `corner` | one of `topLeft`, `topRight`, `bottomLeft`, `bottomRight` | no | bottomRight | bubble: corner of the face (default bottomRight); cutout: bottomLeft or bottomRight. |
| `shape` | one of `circle`, `rounded` | no | – | bubble: circle (default) or rounded (rounded square). |
| `size` | one of `S`, `M`, `L` | no | – | bubble / cutout: S, M (default) or L. |
| `side` | one of `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` | no | – | split: face on the right (default) or left; stack: face at the bottom (default) or top. |
| `frame` | boolean | no | – | screen / bubble: a styled frame — the whole screen (never cropped) on a background with padding, rounded corners and a soft shadow. Implied by any of the frame options below; false removes it. |
| `background` | string | no | when a kit is applied, else graphite | Frame background: a built-in gradient (graphite, aurum, dusk, lagoon, mist, sand; layout.presets describes them), brand (the applied kit's colours: the default when a kit is applied, else graphite), a colour #RRGGBB, or an image file (aspect fill). |
| `gradient` | array of string | no | – | Frame background: a custom gradient of 2–3 colours #RRGGBB (instead of background). |
| `gradientKind` | one of `linear`, `radial` | no | – | Custom gradient: linear (default) or radial (from the centre). |
| `angle` | number | no | – | Linear gradient direction, degrees: 0 towards the top, 90 towards the right, 180 towards the bottom (default). |
| `padding` | number | no | 0.06 | Frame: space around the screen, fraction of the frame's shorter side (default 0.06; 0–0.3). |
| `radius` | number | no | 0.016 | Frame: screen corner radius, fraction of the frame's shorter side (default 0.016; 0 = square corners). |
| `shadow` | number | no | 0.5 | Frame: opacity of the soft shadow under the screen, 0–1 (default 0.5; 0 = none). |

Returns: the recording id, assets, tracks, the common window and the per-source offsets.

### `recording.synthesize`

**Create a test recording** · MCP tool: `recording_synthesize` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Write a synthetic screen-recording session for tests, in exactly the format of a real Registra recording: screen.mov (an animated desktop with an editor and a browser window, the session clock, a moving cursor and click ripples), camera.mov (a stretch of a real camera take), mic.wav (its sound), session.json with sources and their offsets on the common clock, clicks, a keystroke, cursor samples, a pause entry and sync slates (white screen frames, a camera flash frame and a 1 kHz beep at the same session instants). Offsets default to screen 0, camera 0.25 s (7.5 frames: sub-frame on purpose), mic 0.18 s. cursor: false records the take as Registra does with the system cursor hidden: no cursor or ripples in screen.mov, cursorInVideo false, a mouseUp after each click, one drag (press 6.2 s, release 7.0 s) and the cursor kind per sample (pointingHand over the buttons), so the compositor draws the cursor (cursor.style). sources: ["screen"] writes a screen-only take (no camera.mov, no mic.wav: Registra with the camera and microphone switched off). Returns the session path and what it contains.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `directory` | string | yes | – | Folder to write the session into (created; existing files are replaced). |
| `camera` | string | no | – | A camera take with sound (video + audio), e.g. a talking-head .MOV. Required when sources include camera or mic. |
| `sources` | array of string | no | all three | Which sources the session holds: screen, camera, mic (default all three; screen is always there). |
| `cameraIn` | seconds | no | 0 | Where the camera stretch starts in the take, seconds (default 0). |
| `duration` | number | no | 14 | Session length, seconds (default 14). |
| `screenSize` | array of integer | no | [1920, 1080] | [width, height] of screen.mov (default [1920, 1080]). |
| `fps` | integer | no | 60 | Screen frame rate (default 60). |
| `screenOffset` | number | no | 0 | Session time of the first screen frame (default 0). |
| `cameraOffset` | number | no | 0.25 | Session time of the first camera frame (default 0.25). |
| `micOffset` | number | no | 0.18 | Session time of the first mic sample (default 0.18). |
| `syncMarks` | integer | no | 3 | Number of sync slates (default 3). |
| `cursor` | boolean | no | true | Draw the cursor into screen.mov (default true; false = recorded without the system cursor). |

Returns: the session path and what it contains.

Add a kind of video of the user's own (e.g. "YouTube tutorial"): a new sheet in the rules folder, copied from an existing kind (from) or empty under its title; every-video still applies to it. Then project.setKind chooses it for a project. Returns the new sheet.

### `rules.check`

**Check the editing rules** · MCP tool: `rules_check` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Check the edit against the rules of its kind before export (export.render runs it too and refuses while a check fails): no captions while the opening title is on screen, none on the closing logo, a clean pause between the last spoken word and the logo, a logo only at the end, no logo or title over the speaker's face, no text under the minimum size. Each violation has its time and, where a safe one exists, its fix as a command call (one undo step; rules.fix applies them). Warnings do not block. Returns pass, the violations, each check's state (on, number, skipped and why) and the problems of the sheets' headers.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | one of `it`, `en`, `fr`, `pt` | no | sheets read (it, en, fr, pt | Language of the default sheets read (it, en, fr, pt; default: the app's interface language). A sheet the user wrote is the same in every language. |

Returns: pass, the violations, each check's state (on, number, skipped and why) and the problems of the sheets' headers.

### `rules.fix`

**Fix the broken rules** · MCP tool: `rules_fix` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Apply the safe fixes of the failing rule checks, all in one undo step: those of one check, or all of them; the check runs again after each fix (a moved logo changes what the captions must clear). A logo outside the end is kept for the closing seconds only. Violations without a fix (a title over the face, text too small) need an edit. Returns the fixes applied and the check after them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check` | one of `title-captions`, `logo-captions`, `logo-pause`, `logo-end`, `face-clear`, `text-size` | no | – | Fix only this check's violations. |
| `all` | boolean | no | – | Fix every failing check that has a fix. |

Returns: the fixes applied and the check after them.

### `rules.get`

**Read a rule sheet** · MCP tool: `rules_get` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Read one rule sheet: its whole Markdown text (header + prose), the prose alone, the switches its header writes (one line per check between two --- lines: `id: on|off [number]`), the checks as they apply to that kind (defaults, then every-video, then the kind's own lines; source says which), and the header's status (an unknown check or a malformed line is listed with its line number and ignored, never fatal). Returns the sheet.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | yes | – | every-video, a built-in kind or a kind of the user's (rules.list). |
| `language` | one of `it`, `en`, `fr`, `pt` | no | sheets read (it, en, fr, pt | Language of the default sheets read (it, en, fr, pt; default: the app's interface language). A sheet the user wrote is the same in every language. |

Returns: the sheet.

List the editing-rule sheets: every-video (always applies) and one per kind of video — the built-in kinds talking-head-reel, screen-tutorial, voice-over-video, reel-graphics, plus the user's own kinds. Each sheet is a Markdown file the user can edit (Settings › Rules); edited says the user's copy replaces the shipped default. Returns the sheets (kind, title, builtIn, edited, path, the switches written in its header, header status), the folder of the user's sheets and the open project's kind.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |

Returns: the sheets (kind, title, builtIn, edited, path, the switches written in its header, header status), the folder of the user's sheets and the open project's kind.

Delete a kind of video of the user's own (its sheet). Only when the user asked. A project that had it falls back to the kind of its format (rules.check says so). Built-in kinds cannot be removed (rules.reset restores their default). Returns the removed kind.

**Change a rule sheet** · MCP tool: `rules_set` · undo: no — replaces or saves the project (opening or creating one clears the history) · takes `project`

## script

### `script.fromTranscript`

**Script from the transcript** · MCP tool: `script_fromTranscript` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

No script file? Build the script from the transcript: one line per sentence (punctuation, or pauses when the transcript has none), repeated readings of the same sentence (restarts, second takes, false starts) folded into one line so takes.list finds them as takes of it. Each line reports its readings and its level against the take's speech (relativeDB far below 0 = an off-mic voice: another speaker, or chatter between takes). Call it with dryRun: true, read the lines, then again with drop: [line numbers] to leave out chatter that is not part of the video. Sets the script (like script.set) and clears computed takes; then takes.list and edit.autoCut work as with a script. Returns the lines.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | no | the only one with a transcript | Transcribed asset (default: the only one with a transcript). |
| `pause` | number | no | 0.6 without punctuation, 1.0 with | Silence that ends a sentence, seconds (default 0.6 without punctuation, 1.0 with). |
| `drop` | array of integer | no | – | Line numbers (1-based, as listed by a dry run) to leave out of the script. |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | – | Only list the lines, change nothing. |

Returns: the lines.

### `script.prepare`

**Prepare the script** · MCP tool: `script_prepare` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Format a script for reading aloud on the teleprompter, before the shoot: one numbered sentence per take, short display lines (≤ maxChars, default 32), a breath mark " / " after mid-sentence commas/colons/dashes (shown as a subtle gap), keywords flagged *like this* (subtly emphasized; pass the same keywords you will give captions.generate — they are kept in the project for it). Sets the project script (like script.set) unless set: false. Returns the prepared text, its sentences with their display lines, and the keywords.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | no | – | Script text: one sentence (take) per line, or numbered lines. |
| `path` | string | no | – | Read the script from this file instead (a script.md with a "## Testo" section works). |
| `maxChars` | integer | no | 32 | Longest display line in characters (default 32). |
| `keywords` | array of string | no | the ones already flagged, else numbers, acronyms and names | Words to emphasize, as written in the script (multi-word ok, e.g. "nove virgola due"). Default: the ones already flagged, else numbers, acronyms and names. |
| `set` | boolean | no | true when a project is open | Also make it the project script (default true when a project is open). |

Returns: the prepared text, its sentences with their display lines, and the keywords.

### `script.set`

**Set the script** · MCP tool: `script_set` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Give Regista the script the speaker reads, one line per take: pass the text, or a file path (a script.md: the numbered lines of its "## Testo" section are used). The same text drives the teleprompter (markup from script.prepare — continuation lines, " / " breath marks, *keywords* — is understood). Needed by takes.list. Clears computed takes. Returns the lines and keywords.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | no | – | Script text: numbered lines ("1. …") or one sentence per line. |
| `path` | string | no | – | Read the script from this file instead. |

Returns: the lines and keywords.

## sfx

### `sfx.add`

**Add a sound effect** · MCP tool: `sfx_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Place a sound effect at a timeline time on an SFX track (A3; another SFX track is added when effects overlap), by library name (sfx.library: the shipped bank or your folder) or file path, with a volume. Put it on the frame of the visual event (a title landing, a cut, a card pop). Returns the clip and track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | seconds | yes | – | Timeline time of the effect's start. |
| `name` | string | no | – | Library name from sfx.library (e.g. whoosh_fast/crisp, pro_pop_in/round, click/soft). |
| `path` | string | no | – | Audio file instead of a library name. |
| `volume` | number | no | 0.3 | Linear gain (default 0.3; 0.2–0.3 sits under the voice). |
| `gain` | number | no | – | Gain in dB instead of volume. |
| `duration` | seconds | no | – | Cut the effect after this many seconds (fades out the last 30 ms). Effects are always cut at the end of the picture. |

Returns: the clip and track.

### `sfx.checkOnsets`

**Check the sound effects** · MCP tool: `sfx_checkOnsets` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Verify that every sound effect lands on its time in a rendered file: the rest of the mix (voice, music and any other effect sounding in the window: same mixer) is subtracted from the render's sound around each effect, then the effect's first 300 ms from its own onset are matched against that residual (normalized cross-correlation, ±80 ms) at the expected position. Pass: every effect found (correlation ≥ minCorrelation) and within `tolerance` frames (default 1). Returns per-effect lag (ms, frames) and correlation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | Rendered video or audio. |
| `tolerance` | number | no | 1 | Frames (default 1). |
| `minCorrelation` | number | no | 0.5 | An effect whose best match is below this is undetected and fails the check (default 0.5). |

Returns: per-effect lag (ms, frames) and correlation.

### `sfx.library`

**List sound effects** · MCP tool: `sfx_library` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

List the sound effects: the bank shipped with Regista (185 sounds made in code by earshot, MIT: whooshes, UI clicks and taps, pops, impacts and sub drops, risers, chimes and dings, logo stings, glitches, key presses), grouped by use, plus the user's own folder (sfxLibrary in engines.json). Each has a name for sfx.add, its length and what it is for; bank sounds also give the onset and the loudest moment (seconds into the file: put a whoosh's peak on the cut). Taste: sparse, on beats and on-screen events, low volume (0.2–0.3). Returns the effects.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | no | – | Only names or descriptions containing this word. |
| `group` | one of `whoosh`, `ui`, `pop`, `impact`, `rise`, `chime`, `logo`, `glitch`, `typing`, `user` | no | – | Only one group of the bank, or "user" for your own folder. |

Returns: the effects.

### `sfx.onCuts`

**Sound effects on the cuts** · MCP tool: `sfx_onCuts` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Sound effects in one switch: a soft whoosh (from the shipped bank) on the cuts of the main video track, its loudest moment on the cut, at least 3 s apart and at most 6, quiet (volume 0.2); remove: true takes every sound effect off instead. One undo step either way; running it again on a reel that already has effects changes nothing. Returns the effects placed or removed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `remove` | boolean | no | – | Remove every sound effect (the clips of the SFX tracks). |
| `name` | string | no | whoosh_fast/crisp | Library name of the sound (default whoosh_fast/crisp). |
| `volume` | number | no | 0.2 | Linear gain (default 0.2). |

Returns: the effects placed or removed.

## status

### `status.add`

**Add a status card** · MCP tool: `status_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

The 'live editing' status row at the top of a reel (round-3 reference ad): on the left a pill with a pulsing REC dot, a label ("EDITING LIVE") and a running timer; on the right a numbered chapter badge ("02 EFFECTS") that slides in at each chapter. Chapters come from you — one per section of the script, at the second the section starts. timerRate > 1 makes a fast 'session clock' (e.g. 8 = the timer runs 8× real time). Mono type, dark glass pills, brand accent. Returns the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | no | EDITING LIVE | Text after the REC dot (default EDITING LIVE; keep it 1–3 words, the reel's language). |
| `chapters` | array of object | no | – | [{at: timeline seconds, label: "EFFECTS"}, …] — numbered 01, 02… in order. |
| `start` | seconds | no | 0 | Timeline start (default 0). |
| `end` | seconds | no | the end of the picture | Timeline end (default: the end of the picture). |
| `timerStart` | number | no | 0 | Seconds the timer shows at the start (default 0). |
| `timerRate` | number | no | 1 | Timer seconds per real second (default 1). |
| `color` | string | no | the kit's highlight, else #FF7A1A | Accent (#RRGGBB or a brand role; default the kit's highlight, else #FF7A1A). |
| `y` | number | no | 128, just under Instagram's account bar | Top of the row, px on a 1080×1920 frame (default 128, just under Instagram's account bar). |
| `trackId` | string | no | a free one | Overlay track (default: a free one). |

Returns: the clip.

## sticker

### `sticker.add`

**Add a sticker** · MCP tool: `sticker_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Pop an emoji or an SF Symbol over the video: a library sticker (fire, sparkles, eyes, idea, check, cross, rocket, point, laugh, target, heart, clap; symbols seal, star, bolt, arrowDown, tap, warning, bulb, click, bell, thumbsUp), any emoji, or any SF Symbol name, with a size, colour (symbols), optional round badge, position (top band by default) and a pop (default) or bounce entrance. Taste: one sticker on a punchline, short (1–1.5 s), never in the caption band. Returns the clip and its box with layout warnings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sticker` | one of `fire`, `sparkles`, `eyes`, `idea`, `check`, `cross`, `rocket`, `point`, `laugh`, `target`, `heart`, `clap`, `seal`, `star`, `bolt`, `arrowDown`, `tap`, `warning`, `bulb`, `click`, `bell`, `thumbsUp` | no | – | Library sticker. |
| `emoji` | string | no | – | An emoji instead. |
| `symbol` | string | no | – | An SF Symbol name instead (e.g. checkmark.seal.fill). |
| `start` | seconds | yes | – | Timeline start. |
| `duration` | seconds | no | 1.4 | Seconds on screen (default 1.4). Left out, the graphic ends with the main video at the latest: shortened, or started earlier to keep 1 s (the result's timing says so). |
| `end` | seconds | no | – | Timeline end instead of duration. |
| `size` | number | no | 160 | Glyph height, px at 1080 wide (default 160). |
| `color` | string | no | – | Symbol colour (#RRGGBB or a brand colour role). |
| `badge` | string | no | – | Round badge colour behind the glyph (#RRGGBB or a brand role). |
| `trackId` | string | no | a free one | Overlay track (default: a free one). |
| `band` | one of `top`, `middle`, `lower` | no | for titles and cards | Vertical band of a 9:16 reel: top (y 110–640, the default for titles and cards), middle, lower (980–1200, just above the captions). The caption band 1230–1460 is reserved. |
| `position` | array of number | no | – | Centre [x, y] in pixels of a 1080×1920 frame (overrides band). |
| `top` | number | no | – | Top edge, pixels of a 1080×1920 frame (instead of a centre). |
| `scale` | number | no | – | Size factor (1 = native size). |
| `opacity` | number | no | 1 | 0…1 (default 1). |
| `rotation` | number | no | – | Degrees clockwise. |
| `animIn` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | – | Entrance: pop (scale with overshoot), slideUp, slideDown, fade, kenBurns (slow push over the whole clip), none. |
| `animOut` | one of `pop`, `slideUp`, `slideDown`, `fade`, `kenBurns`, `bounce`, `none` | no | same as animIn | Exit (default: same as animIn; kenBurns has none). |
| `inDuration` | number | no | 0.35 | Entrance seconds (default 0.35; fade 0.25). |
| `outDuration` | number | no | 0.25 | Exit seconds (default 0.25). |

Returns: the clip and its box with layout warnings.

## style

### `style.apply`

**Apply a style** · MCP tool: `style_apply` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

One-click style: a bundle of ordinary edits, undone as one step, in the active brand kit's colours. energico (Reel energico): a vivid look, alternating punch-in framing per sentence (clip), a soft whoosh on a few cuts (≥ 3 s apart, max 6), word-by-word pop captions. pulito (Pulito): a light airy look, gentle contrast and sharpness, calm chunk captions, no sound effects. tutorial: auto-zoom on the recording's clicks with a circle callout on each (screen recordings), a progress bar, crisp picture. console (Console): the whole reel as a 'live editing console' — dark grid + glow backdrop (background-scene), the speaker in a neon inset card (PREVIEW chip, brand accent glow), the status row with REC timer and numbered chapters (pass chapters, one per script section), bold-keyword captions in the accent. intensity scales every move (default 0.6). Returns what was applied and what was skipped (and why).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | one of `energico`, `pulito`, `tutorial`, `console` | yes | – | Style. |
| `intensity` | number | no | 0.6 | 0…1 (default 0.6). |
| `chapters` | array of object | no | – | console: [{at: seconds, label}] for the status row's chapter badge (status.add). |
| `label` | string | no | EDITING LIVE | console: text after the REC dot (default EDITING LIVE). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first one | Main video track (default: the first one). |

Returns: what was applied and what was skipped (and why).

## takes

### `takes.compare`

**Compare takes** · MCP tool: `takes_compare` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Test helper: compare the video track's cuts with a hand edit (a segments.json of source in/out per segment): for every script line, whether the same take was used and the in/out error in ms. Returns the per-line comparison.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reference` | string | yes | – | Path of the reference segments.json. |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first video track | Video track holding the cut (default: the first video track). |

Returns: the per-line comparison.

### `takes.list`

**Find the takes** · MCP tool: `takes_list` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Find every reading of every script line (the speaker repeats a line until it comes out right), pick the best per line (complete, no restart; the last complete one by default) and compute its cut points on the speech envelope. A teleprompter recording's live take markers are used first (the restarts were seen live); otherwise the transcript is aligned to the script. Show this list to the user as text. Returns the source (live / transcript) and per line: the takes (text, start/end, complete or not, word error rate) and the chosen one; then use takes.select to override and edit.autoCut to build.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | no | the only one with a transcript or live take markers | Transcribed asset (default: the only one with a transcript or live take markers). |
| `source` | one of `auto`, `live`, `transcript` | no | – | auto (default): live markers when the asset has them for this script, else the transcript. |
| `maxWer` | number | no | 0.3 | Word error rate still counted as complete (default 0.3). |
| `maxPause` | number | no | 0.7 | Pauses longer than this inside a take are cut out, seconds (default 0.7). |
| `keepPause` | number | no | 0.12 | Silence kept on each side of a removed pause, seconds (default 0.12). |
| `pre` | number | no | 0.10 | Lead-in before speech, seconds (default 0.10). |
| `post` | number | no | 0.20 | Tail after speech, seconds (default 0.20). |

Returns: the source (live / transcript) and per line: the takes (text, start/end, complete or not, word error rate) and the chosen one; then use takes.select to override and edit.autoCut to build.

### `takes.live`

**Takes marked by the teleprompter** · MCP tool: `takes_live` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Attach the teleprompter's live take markers to a recording (normally automatic: media.import reads the <name>.takes.json the app writes next to each recording). Pass a markers file (the app's sidecar or a teleprompter.simulate output), or clear: true. takes.list then prefers them. Returns the markers per line and whether they match the project script.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | no | the only video asset | Recording asset (default: the only video asset). |
| `path` | string | no | – | JSON with {sentences, markers: [{sentence, take, start, end, complete}]}. |
| `clear` | boolean | no | – | Remove the asset's live markers. |

Returns: the markers per line and whether they match the project script.

### `takes.select`

**Pick a take** · MCP tool: `takes_select` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Override the take edit.autoCut uses for a script line (1-based line and take, as in takes.list) when the automatic pick has a stumble, a cut-off ending or a weaker reading; auto: true restores the automatic pick. Then run edit.autoCut with replace: true. Returns the line's choice.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `line` | integer | yes | – | Script line, 1-based. |
| `take` | integer | no | – | Take number, 1-based. |
| `auto` | boolean | no | – | Restore the automatic pick. |

Returns: the line's choice.

## teleprompter

### `teleprompter.simulate`

**Try the teleprompter** · MCP tool: `teleprompter_simulate` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Test the teleprompter without a speaker: replays an audio/video file through the live on-device recognizer (Apple SpeechTranscriber, else SFSpeechRecognizer) at speed× real time and drives the take tracker with it, as if the speaker were reading the script. Returns the cursor lag (median/p90 ms between a word ending and the confirmed cursor / the drawn highlight, with its lead, reaching it), the restarts seen, the live take markers and, with a reference segments.json, which lines got the same take as the hand edit. Writes the full log (cursor moves, restarts, markers; usable by takes.live) to output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | string | no | – | Audio or video file (the take). |
| `replay` | string | no | – | Instead of audio: an earlier simulate log — replays its recognizer updates offline (deterministic, no speech engine needed). |
| `script` | string | yes | – | Script file (script.md works) or the script text. |
| `language` | string | no | it-IT | Recognizer locale (default it-IT; fr-FR for French). |
| `speed` | number | no | – | Feed speed, 1 = real time (default; lag numbers are only meaningful at 1). |
| `engine` | one of `DictationTranscriber`, `SpeechTranscriber`, `SFSpeechRecognizer` | no | the teleprompter's, DictationTranscriber on macOS 26 | Recognizer (default: the teleprompter's, DictationTranscriber on macOS 26). |
| `reference` | string | no | – | segments.json of the hand edit (source in/out per segment), to compare the takes. |
| `output` | string | no | a temporary file | Where to write the log JSON (default: a temporary file). |

Returns: the cursor lag (median/p90 ms between a word ending and the confirmed cursor / the drawn highlight, with its lead, reaching it), the restarts seen, the live take markers and, with a reference segments.json, which lines got the same take as the hand edit. Writes the full log (cursor moves, restarts, markers; usable by takes.live) to output.

## timeline

### `timeline.cut`

**Cut** · MCP tool: `timeline_cut` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Razor: split clips at a timeline time (e.g. before deleting a piece). The left part keeps the clip id, the right part gets a new id (right parts of linked clips stay linked together). Without clipId/trackId, cuts every unlocked track that has a clip there; with them, the linked clips are cut too. Returns the new clip ids.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | seconds | yes | – | Timeline time of the cut. |
| `clipId` | string | no | – | Only cut this clip (and its linked clips). |
| `trackId` | string | no | – | Only cut the clip of this track (and its linked clips). |
| `linked` | boolean | no | true | Also act on the clips linked to it (picture/sound of the same take), default true. |

Returns: the new clip ids.

### `timeline.delete`

**Delete** · MCP tool: `timeline_delete` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Remove clips and the clips linked to them. With ripple, the following clips of each affected track move left to close the gap (other tracks are not touched). For removing words prefer transcript.deleteWords. Returns what was removed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | no | – | One clip id. |
| `clipIds` | array of string | no | – | Several clip ids. |
| `ripple` | boolean | no | false | Close the gap left by each clip (default false). |
| `linked` | boolean | no | true | Also act on the clips linked to it (picture/sound of the same take), default true. |

Returns: what was removed.

### `timeline.duplicate`

**Duplicate** · MCP tool: `timeline_duplicate` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Copy clips to another time on their own tracks (duplicate, or copy and paste at the playhead): every property comes along (position, grade, effects, speed, fades, gain, a title's text, a motion template's fields), the copies get new ids, and copies of clips linked together are linked together. Linked clips come along unless linked: false. Fails if a spot is occupied. Returns the new clips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipIds` | array of string | yes | – | Clips to copy. |
| `start` | seconds | no | right after the last of the clips, or after the end of their tracks when that spot is taken | Where the earliest copy begins (default: right after the last of the clips, or after the end of their tracks when that spot is taken). |
| `linked` | boolean | no | true | Also act on the clips linked to it (picture/sound of the same take), default true. |

Returns: the new clips.

### `timeline.link`

**Link clips** · MCP tool: `timeline_link` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Link clips (e.g. a picture clip and its sound) so place/move/trim/cut/delete act on all of them, or unlink them to edit picture and sound separately. Returns the link id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipIds` | array of string | yes | – | Clips to link together (or to unlink). |
| `unlink` | boolean | no | false | Remove these clips from their link instead (default false). |

Returns: the link id.

### `timeline.mapTimes`

**Convert times** · MCP tool: `timeline_mapTimes` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Translate times between a reference edit (its segments.json: source ranges played back to back) and this timeline through the source frames they show — to put graphics, inserts and SFX of a hand-made edit at the same moments of the speech (toTimeline), or to find the reference frame of a timeline moment (toReference). A time whose source frame was cut goes to the nearest kept frame (exact: false). Returns the mapped times.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `referenceSegments` | string | yes | – | The reference's segments.json. |
| `times` | array of number | yes | – | Times to map, seconds. |
| `direction` | one of `toTimeline`, `toReference` | no | toTimeline | Default toTimeline. |
| `trackId` | string | no | the first video track | Video track of this timeline (default: the first video track). |

Returns: the mapped times.

### `timeline.move`

**Move** · MCP tool: `timeline_move` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Move a clip to another time and optionally another track of a compatible kind; linked clips move by the same amount on their own tracks. Fails if a spot is occupied. Returns the moved clips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | – | Clip id. |
| `start` | seconds | yes | – | New timeline start. |
| `trackId` | string | no | same track | Destination track (default: same track). |
| `linked` | boolean | no | true | Also act on the clips linked to it (picture/sound of the same take), default true. |

Returns: the moved clips.

### `timeline.place`

**Put on the timeline** · MCP tool: `timeline_place` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Manual editing: place an asset (or a source range of it) on a track as a new clip at a timeline time, optionally linked to another clip. Fails if the spot is occupied. Returns the new clip id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes | – | Asset id from media.import. |
| `trackId` | string | yes | – | Target track id. |

Returns: the new clip id.

### `timeline.trim`

**Trim** · MCP tool: `timeline_trim` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Move the start or end edge of a clip to a timeline time, revealing or hiding source media (tighten a pause, restore a clipped word). Linked clips whose same edge sits at the same time follow. With ripple, later clips on the track shift to keep their distance. Returns the changed clips.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | – | Clip id. |
| `edge` | one of `start`, `end` | yes | – | Which edge to move. |
| `to` | seconds | yes | – | New timeline time of that edge. |
| `ripple` | boolean | no | false | Shift the following clips of the track by the change (default false). A rippled start trim keeps the clip's start in place. |
| `linked` | boolean | no | true | Also act on the clips linked to it (picture/sound of the same take), default true. |

Returns: the changed clips.

## transcript

### `transcript.deleteWords`

**Remove words from the edit** · MCP tool: `transcript_deleteWords` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Text-based editing: remove a range of words (indices from transcript.timeline, inclusive) from the timeline — a stumble, a filler, a repeated word. Cuts every video/audio track at the range edges (frame-snapped) and ripple-deletes the pieces in between, one undo step; captions, if any, are regenerated. Re-run edit.punchIns afterwards if the clip pattern changed. Returns the commands it ran.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |

| `from` | integer | yes | – | First word index to remove. |
| `to` | integer | no | from | Last word index to remove (default: from). |

| `expect` | string | no | – | Safety check: the removed words must read this (case and punctuation ignored). |

Returns: the commands it ran.

### `transcript.editText`

**Correct the transcript** · MCP tool: `transcript_editText` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Correct what was said in the text (a misheard name, a typo): replace the words from…to (indices from transcript.timeline, inclusive) with new text. Only the text changes — the picture and the timing stay; the new words share the old words' time span in proportion to their length. Captions, if any, are regenerated. Empty text hides those words from the captions. Returns the old and new text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | integer | yes | – | First word index. |
| `to` | integer | no | from | Last word index (default: from). |
| `text` | string | yes | – | The corrected text for that range. |
| `trackId` | string | no | as transcript.timeline | Track whose words the indices refer to (default: as transcript.timeline). |
| `expect` | string | no | – | Safety check: the words being replaced must read this (case and punctuation ignored). |

Returns: the old and new text.

Diagnostics: word-timing accuracy of an asset's transcript against the audio energy envelope at every pause (word starts vs speech onsets, ends vs offsets). For tuning engines, not needed in a normal edit. Returns medians and percentiles in ms.

Read the transcript of an asset: words with start/end seconds (asset/source time) and the full text, optionally only [from, to]. Use it to find a stumble or a misheard name. Returns {words, text}.
