**Transcribe** · MCP tool: `transcript_run` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Transcribe an asset with word timings (extracts its audio first if needed): needed by takes.list, captions and text-based editing. Engines: whisper.cpp (Base tier) or whisperx (Medium tier and up, more precise word timings); the default depends on the RAM tier (whisper.cpp, with a note, when the tier's engine is not installed). Cached by audio hash. Returns word count, engine, the text and a note when the engine was not the one expected.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assetId` | string | yes | – | Asset to transcribe. |
| `engine` | one of `whisper.cpp`, `whisperx` | no | per tier | Transcription engine (default: per tier). |
| `language` | string | no | "it" | Spoken language code (default "it"); "auto" detects it (whisper.cpp; with whisperx the language is detected first, then aligned). |
| `cache` | boolean | no | true | Reuse a cached transcript of the same audio and engine (default true). |

Returns: word count, engine, the text and a note when the engine was not the one expected.

### `transcript.timeline`

**Timeline transcript** · MCP tool: `transcript_timeline` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

The words as the timeline now plays them, with an index per word and the clip it belongs to. Use it to find a repeated word, a filler or a stumble left in the edit, then remove it with transcript.deleteWords. Returns {count, text, words: [{i, text, start, end, clip}]}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trackId` | string | no | the first video track with clips | Track to read (default: the first video track with clips). |

Returns: {count, text, words: [{i, text, start, end, clip}]}.

## transition

### `transition.add`

**Add a transition** · MCP tool: `transition_add` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Add a frame-wide transition at a cut: flash (white wash peaking on the cut, 0.2 s), whip (the picture flies out and the next one in with motion blur, 0.3 s) dip (through black, 0.5 s) or blur (the picture defocuses into the cut and the next shot comes back into focus, 0.6 s; also into or out of a full-frame graphic). Anchor it to a clip edge (clipId + edge: it follows later edits) or a timeline time. Captions are not affected. Taste: one or two per reel, on real section changes. Returns the transition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `flash`, `whip`, `dip`, `blur` | yes | – | flash, whip, dip or blur. |
| `at` | seconds | no | – | Cut time on the timeline. |
| `clipId` | string | no | – | Anchor clip (its start, or its end with edge: end). |
| `edge` | one of `start`, `end` | no | start | Edge of clipId (default start). |
| `duration` | seconds | no | – | Total length centred on the cut (defaults: flash 0.2, whip 0.3, dip 0.5, blur 0.6). |
| `direction` | one of `left`, `right`, `up`, `down` | no | left | whip: where the picture leaves to (default left). |
| `color` | string | no | #FFFFFF | flash colour (default #FFFFFF). |

Returns: the transition.

### `transition.remove`

**Remove a transition** · MCP tool: `transition_remove` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Remove a transition (transitionId from transition.add or project.state). Returns the remaining count.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `transitionId` | string | yes | – | Transition id. |

Returns: the remaining count.

## ui

### `ui.screenshot`

**Look at the window** · MCP tool: `ui_screenshot` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

See the Regista app the way the user sees it: renders the app window (an activity of its left bar, or the editor: "edit-pro" = monitors and timeline, "edit-semplice" = the guided steps of the simple level) to a PNG, returned as an image. Only when the app is running. Returns the path, size and what the window shows (timeline lanes and clip counts).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | one of `home`, `record`, `media`, `texts`, `audio`, `voice`, `graphics`, `generate`, `export`, `edit-pro`, `edit-semplice`, `pro`, `semplice`, `panel-prompter`, `panel-claude`, `panel-inspector`, `settings`, `teleprompter`, `teleprompter-mirror`, `brand-picker`, `pro-fullscreen`, `graphics-filters`, `graphics-adjust`, `graphics-effects`, `graphics-styles`, `graphics-motion`, `graphics-logo`, `voice-setup`, `settings-voice`, `settings-general`, `settings-engines`, `settings-engines-base`, `settings-engines-medium`, `settings-engines-pro`, `settings-brand`, `settings-rules`, `settings-claude`, `settings-shortcuts`, `help`, `help-voice`, `help-install`, `help-troubleshooting`, `export-rules`, `export-rules-pass` | no | the current one | Workspace to show (default: the current one; the app switches back afterwards). The window is an activity bar on the left (home = Inizio: ways in, recent projects; record = Registra; media, texts, audio, voice, graphics, generate = the editor with that library activity in the side panel; export = Esporta), project tabs on top, and a right panel (Gobbo, Claude, Ispettore). edit-pro (also pro, pro-fullscreen) = the editor at the Pro level, edit-semplice (also semplice) = its simple level: six guided steps (cut and takes, captions, look, music and sounds, voice, graphics) beside one monitor; panel-prompter / panel-claude / panel-inspector = edit-pro with that right-panel tab; settings = the Settings window (720×600) on its Generale tab; settings-general / settings-engines / settings-voice / settings-brand (the brand kit editor) / settings-rules (the editing rules, from sample sheets) / settings-claude / settings-shortcuts = that tab; settings-engines-base / -medium / -pro = the Motori tab as on that tier (the Mac's real engine states, the tier only for the render: engines.json is not touched; shown reports the tier, the rows that need a higher tier and the installable ones). teleprompter / teleprompter-mirror render the speaker's teleprompter window (normally invisible to screen capture) with the project script, default 640×360. brand-picker = the Marca picker (the one place that picks the project's kit; 300 wide). graphics-filters / -adjust / -effects / -styles / -motion / -logo = the Graphics activity on that section of its panel (looks, adjustments, effects, one-click styles, motion templates, logo), the editor in the main area. voice = the editor with the Voce activity, voice-setup = the Gestisci voci window (880×620: the four languages with their state, the selected language's tones and training, or its intro, consent, recording and check), settings-voice = Settings › Profilo e voce (720×600): all three drawn from `voice` (sample data, never the real profile) or, without it, from the live state. export-rules / export-rules-pass = Esporta with the editing rules' card from a sample report (two rules failing with their fixes / everything passing). help = the help window (Aiuto menu, 960×700) on the user guide, help-voice / help-install / help-troubleshooting on that guide, in the app's language, from the guides shipped in the app. |
| `size` | array of integer | no | the current size | Window size in points [width, height], e.g. [1440, 900] (default: the current size). |
| `path` | string | no | a temporary file | Output .png (default: a temporary file). |
| `canvas` | object | no | – | Show a selection on the preview as if clicked/dragged (pro or semplice, at the playhead — preview.frame moves it): {select: "caption" \| <clipId>, drag?: [dx, dy] frame pixels (snap guides and the red Instagram zones show), scale?: factor, scope?: "all" \| "one"}. |
| `voice` | object | no | – | With workspace voice / voice-setup / settings-voice: draw that screen from sample data, for the render only: {state: panel "engine-missing" \| "no-profile" \| "no-voice" (the way into cloning) \| "one-tone" \| "ready" (several tones, trained) \| "hint" (the training hint) \| "rendering" \| "placed" \| "lexicon" \| "imported" (a voice trained outside the app, no recorded minutes); window "profile" \| "intro" (a new language) \| "consent" \| "record" (another tone) \| "check-good" \| "check-poor" \| "overview" \| "overview-low-ram" \| "training" \| "imported"; settings: any panel state, tier?: "base" \| "medium" \| "pro" (forced RAM tier)}. |
| `real` | boolean | no | – | true: capture the real window as it is on screen, the native title bar and traffic lights included (ScreenCaptureKit; needs the Screen Recording permission already granted to Regista — it never asks, it fails with an error instead). Not combinable with workspace, size, canvas, record or voice. shown reports windowHeight, titleRowHeight (the native toolbar band), the three trafficLightButtons frames, contentTop (where the activity bar, side panel and project tabs begin) and titleItems (the toolbar item with Claude's status and the panel toggles). |
| `inspector` | object | no | – | Show the Ispettore tab of the right panel (with the Pro editor unless workspace says otherwise) for a selection, drawn without clicking and without changing the real selection: {select: <clipId> \| "first-video" \| "first-audio" \| "first-music" \| "first-overlay" \| "captions" \| "multi" (the first two video clips) \| "none", project?: path of a .regista folder opened for this render only (a scratch copy: the open tabs and their projects are not touched)}. shown.inspector reports what the panel shows (kind, clips, sections). |
| `texts` | object | no | – | With workspace "texts": draw the Passi of Testi e sottotitoli (from an imported clip to captions) from sample data, for the render only: {state: "fresh" \| "transcribing" \| "transcribed" \| "cut" \| "keywords" \| "captions" \| "stale" \| "doall" \| "failed", tier?: "base" \| "medium" \| "pro"}. shown.steps reports each step's status. |
| `simple` | object | no | the next one to do | With workspace "edit-semplice": the Semplice level's six steps, for the render only: {step?: "cut" \| "captions" \| "look" \| "sound" \| "voice" \| "graphics" (the step open; default the next one to do), state?: "midway" (cut and captions done, two lines with retakes) \| "done" (every step in place) \| "doall" (Fai tutto running on its third step) — sample states drawn over the project shown; without state, the project's real states}. shown.simple reports each step's status and the step open. |
| `generate` | object | no | – | With workspace "generate": the Genera side panel from sample data, for the render only (nothing is run, priced or approved): {state: "still" \| "clip" \| "music" \| "upscale" (that kind ready to run, with sample providers: ComfyUI local and Higgsfield paid) \| "unavailable" (a Mac with no generator set up: each provider greyed with its reason and the install / setup link) \| "approval" (a paid clip's cost on the approval card) \| "running" (a clip being generated, with progress and Cancel) \| "failed" (a run that went wrong, in words) \| "recent" (the project's recent generations), kind?: still \| clip \| music \| upscale}. shown.generate reports the kind, the providers with their availability and the state. |
| `jobs` | object | no | – | Draw sample jobs in the status bar's jobs item (a transcription, an export, a "Fai tutto" with sub-steps, a failed and a finished job, in two tabs): {open?: true (default) \| false — the jobs list drawn open above the item}. |
| `audio` | object | no | – | With workspace "audio": draw the Audio activity for the render only: {tab?: "mix" \| "sfx" (the sound-effect browser), group?: whoosh \| ui \| pop \| impact \| rise \| chime \| logo \| glitch \| typing \| user \| all (the open group), query?: a search, loudness?: [integrated LUFS, true peak dBTP] (sample level instead of the meter's), check?: {pass, underDB, minUnder} (a sample ducking check), playing?: a sound name drawn as playing}. Combine with inspector.project to draw a project opened for the render only. |
| `tabs` | integer | no | the tabs open in the app | Draw this many project tabs on top of the main area (1–12): the active tab, then sample tabs (unsaved, recording, saved), to see the tab strip without opening other projects. Default: the tabs open in the app. |
| `record` | object | no | – | With workspace "record": draw the Registra screen in this state for the render only (the recorder and the saved choices do not change): {preset?: "screen-only" \| "screen-face" \| "face" \| "voice", screen?, camera?, microphone?, systemAudio?, prompter?: booleans (after the preset), open?: "screen" \| "camera" \| "microphone" (that row's choices open), layout?: bubble \| split \| stack \| face \| cutout \| screen, corner?, size?, shape?, permissions?: "actual" (default) \| "granted" (as if macOS allowed camera, microphone and screen), displays?: 1–4 (sample displays instead of the connected ones, the first one main and the second one selected: with two or more the display picker shows under the Schermo row)}. shown.record reports the preset, the switches and each row as drawn. |

Returns: the path, size and what the window shows (timeline lanes and clip counts).

## voice

### `voice.enroll.add`

**Record a voice sample** · MCP tool: `voice_enroll_add` · undo: no — replaces or saves the project (opening or creating one clears the history) · takes `project`

Add one recording of a tone block to the active profile's voice: transcribes it, checks the consent sentence (first take of a language), finds each script line, cuts one clip per line heard and picks a reference clip for the tone. After the neutral block the language works at once in zero-shot. Takes a minute or two per 10 min of audio. Returns {accepted, total, missing, reference, minutes}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | – | The recording (any audio or video file: phone memo, Regista take). |
| `language` | string | yes | – | Language of the script read. |
| `tone` | one of `neutral`, `enthusiastic`, `serious`, `calm`, `playful`, `alarmed`, `sad` | yes | – | The block read in this file. |

Returns: {accepted, total, missing, reference, minutes}.

### `voice.enroll.script`

**Voice enrolment text** · MCP tool: `voice_enroll_script` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Start recording the active profile's own voice: the recording script of a language (consent sentence with their name, then 7 tone blocks: neutral ~10 min, enthusiastic, serious, calm, playful, alarmed, sad ~2 min each), also written to script.md in the profile so they can read it from a phone. Recording advice: a phone with an external mic in a soft, quiet room is best; one file per block. Then voice.enroll.add per file. Returns {consent, blocks, file, minutes}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | yes | – | fr, it, en or pt. |

Returns: {consent, blocks, file, minutes}.

### `voice.enroll.status`

**Voice status** · MCP tool: `voice_enroll_status` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Where the active profile's voice stands per language: consent, minutes and clips per tone, zero-shot ready, training running / done / failed. A finished training registers its LoRA here. Returns {profile, languages}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | no | all recorded | One language (default: all recorded). |

Returns: {profile, languages}.

### `voice.enroll.train`

**Train the voice** · MCP tool: `voice_enroll_train` · undo: no — replaces or saves the project (opening or creating one clears the history) · takes `project`

Train the active profile's voice LoRA for a language in the background (VoxCPM2 trainer, Pro tier): ~10 min of clips → about 2 h on an M5 Pro; a 2-minute pilot → ~10 min. Poll voice.enroll.status; when it ends the LoRA is used automatically. Returns {status, estimatedMinutes}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | yes | – | Language to train. |

Returns: {status, estimatedMinutes}.

### `voice.lexicon`

**Pronunciation** · MCP tool: `voice_lexicon` · undo: no — replaces or saves the project (opening or creating one clears the history) · takes `project`

The active profile's pronunciation lexicon for a language: how words the model mispronounces must be written for it (brand names keep their original pronunciation, never translated or adapted). Lists entries; `add` {word, say} with status confirmed (approved by ear) or pending (chosen by a Whisper read-back, waiting for the person's ear); `remove` a word. Applied only to the text sent to the model; captions keep the real spelling. Returns the entries.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | yes | – | fr, it, en, pt… |
| `add` | object | no | – | {"word": "WeSites", "say": "We Sites"}. |
| `status` | one of `confirmed`, `pending` | no | pending: confirmed only after the person listened | Status of the added entry (default pending: confirmed only after the person listened). |
| `remove` | string | no | – | Word to remove. |

Returns: the entries.

### `voice.list`

**List voices** · MCP tool: `voice_list` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

The active profile's cloned voice before a voice-over: per language, LoRA or zero-shot, the tones it can say, the reference clips, the pronunciation lexicon and any missing file; plus whether the VoxCPM2 engine can run here. Only the active profile's voice is ever usable. Then render with generate.run {kind: "voice", prompt: <text>, options: {language, tone}}. Returns {profile, languages, engine}.

No parameters.

Returns: {profile, languages, engine}.

### `voice.preview`

**Listen to the voice** · MCP tool: `voice_preview` · undo: no — reads only · takes `project`

Hear a voice-over before placing it: renders the paragraphs of `text` (or only paragraph `paragraph`) in the active profile's voice, without touching the project or the timeline, and returns the audio files. voice.say with the same text, language and tone reuses these renders (nothing is rendered twice). `estimate: true` renders nothing: the paragraphs with their estimated duration and whether each is already rendered. Returns {paragraphs: [{index, text, file?, seconds, cached}], seconds, renderSeconds}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | – | What to say. Paragraphs separated by a blank line (as voice.say). |
| `language` | string | yes | – | Language of the text (fr, it, en, pt). |
| `tone` | string | no | – | neutral (default) or a tone the voice has (voice.list). |
| `seed` | integer | no | – | As voice.say. |
| `paragraph` | integer | no | – | Only this paragraph (0-based). |
| `estimate` | boolean | no | – | Render nothing: estimated durations and what is already rendered. |

Returns: {paragraphs: [{index, text, file?, seconds, cached}], seconds, renderSeconds}.

### `voice.say`

**Voice-over** · MCP tool: `voice_say` · undo: yes — one undo step · takes `project`

Voice-over in the active profile's own voice, placed on the timeline: splits the text into paragraphs (blank lines), renders each one whole (VoxCPM2, cached), lays them on the «Voce» audio track from `at` with `gap` seconds between paragraphs, and gives every clip word timings with the real spelling of the text, so captions.generate {sourceTrackId: <Voce track>} needs no transcription. Write numbers in words and brand names as they are spelled (the pronunciation lexicon fixes how they are said). One undo step. Returns the track, clips, total duration and the AI-disclosure reminder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | – | What to say. Paragraphs separated by a blank line. |
| `language` | string | yes | – | Language of the text (fr, it, en, pt): the profile must have that voice (voice.list). |
| `tone` | string | no | – | neutral (default) or a tone the voice has (voice.list). |
| `at` | seconds | no | the end of the Voce track, or 0 | Timeline start (default: the end of the Voce track, or 0). |
| `gap` | number | no | 0.35 | Seconds of silence between paragraphs (default 0.35). |
| `trackId` | string | no | the «Voce» track, created if missing | Audio track to use (default: the «Voce» track, created if missing). |
| `seed` | integer | no | derived from each paragraph's text | Seed of the first paragraph (+1 per paragraph); default derived from each paragraph's text. |
| `replace` | array of string | no | – | The clips an earlier voice.say placed for this text, one per paragraph in order (its result's clips): the text is placed again over them — a changed paragraph replaces its clip in place (a new clip id), an unchanged one keeps its clip, the clips after a paragraph that got longer or shorter move by the difference, a new paragraph at the end goes after the last voice, a removed one takes its clip away. Not with at. |

Returns: the track, clips, total duration and the AI-disclosure reminder.
